jobs.title: Tenure-Track Assistant Professor of Communication
statuses: Job description: The Department of Communication at Rollins College invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Communication beginning August 2027. We seek a scholar-teacher who uses high-impact educational practices to prepare students for responsible leadership and global citizenship, including service learning, community engagement, interdisciplinary collaboration, and student-faculty research. The successful candidate will teach foundational courses in the Communication major, including COM 100: Introduction to Communication, COM 285: Research Methods, and/or COM 480: Senior Seminar (capstone course), and will have the opportunity to develop electives in their area of expertise. Areas of interest may include persuasion, communication theory, civic engagement, crisis communication, digital media, artificial intelligence and emerging communication technologies, or other areas where communication intersects with global challenges. The successful candidate will also contribute to the College’s general education program.

jobs.title: Professor of Practice, Operations, Technology, and Information Management
jobs.snippet: Professor of Practice, Operations, Technology, and Information Management Cornell SC Johnson College of Business Cornell University The Cornell SC Johnson College of Business invites applicants for a Professor of Practice position with 50 – 100% appointment in our Operations, Technology, and Information Management (OTIM) area, with a school affiliation in the Johnson Graduate School of Management.
jobs.detailText: Professor of Practice, Operations, Technology, and Information Management Cornell SC Johnson College of Business Cornell University The Cornell SC Johnson College of Business invites applicants for a Professor of Practice position with 50 – 100% appointment in our Operations, Technology, and Information Management (OTIM) area, with a school affiliation in the Johnson Graduate School of Management. The intended start date of this position is July 1, 2027. The position will be based in Ithaca, NY. Responsibilities of the position include teaching MBA courses in Operations Strategy, Experience in Strategic Operations, and other related graduate courses in the college. The ideal candidate will possess a PhD in business or a related field and have relevant prior work experience in a senior leadership role in industry. Candidates holding a master's degree in business or a closely related field, along with relevant teaching experience, will also be considered. It is expected that our faculty teach across multiple schools within the College of Business. The Cornell SC Johnson College of Business (established on July 1, 2016) combines three Schools: the Samuel Curtis Johnson Graduate School of Management (Johnson), the Charles H. Dyson School of Applied Economics and Management (Dyson), and the Nolan School of Hotel Administration (Nolan). The Samuel Curtis Johnson Graduate School of Management offers MBA, Accelerated MBA, Executive MBA, and Ph.D. programs. Courses and programs are taught at Cornell's main Ithaca campus, the Cornell Tech campus in New York City, and other locations across the globe. To be considered for this position, apply at https://academicjobsonline.org/ajo/jobs/33006 . For full consideration please ensure that your application is complete by October 31, 2026. Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position has been filled. Applications received after October 31, 2026 will be reviewed if the position has not been filled. The following materials are required: 1. Letter of interest, with clear indication of position being applied for; 2. Curriculum vitae; 3. Up to three research papers; 4. Three recommendation letters; 5. Report of courses taught and evidence of teaching effectiveness; and 6. Any other supporting documents, such as curriculum development materials Consistent with Cornell's practice, appointment to academic positions requires candidates to disclose relevant information about their prior employment including whether they have been found to have violated institutional or employer policies related to or governing unlawful discrimination and harassment, academic and research misconduct, or financial misconduct. In compliance with New York's Pay Transparency Act, the minimum annual base salary range for this position is $120,000 - $280,000. This pay range represents base pay only (for 9 months, paid over 12 months) and excludes any additional items such as incentives, bonuses, or other items. Cornell University considers factors such as (but not limited to) scope and responsibilities of the position, candidate's work experience, education/training, key skills, internal peer equity, as well as market and organizational considerations when extending an offer. Part-time Faculty Positions DePaul University invites expressions of interest for a pool of qualified Part Time Faculty to teach courses in a variety of disciplines across all 10 colleges and schools. Individuals may enter expressions of interest by submitting their credentials to any posting for which they are qualified to teach. Postings are organized by college/school and department. Part-time teaching opportunities fluctuate from quarter to quarter throughout the academic year. The applicants with expertise that match the course scheduling needs will be contacted for an interview. The School will work with selected individuals to determine their schedule. Courses are not guaranteed; however, the School does its best to give ample notice about available classes or potential course cancellations. The salary offered to the selected candidate will be determined based on factors such as (but not limited to) the qualifications, education, experience, and training of the selected candidate, the scope and responsibilities of the position, departmental budget availability, internal salary equity considerations, and available market information. DePaul University offers a variety of benefit options for qualified part-time employees. Further information regarding benefits can be found here: https://offices.depaul.edu/human-resources/benefits/part-time/Pages/default.aspx About DePaul University's Academic Calendar: Except for the College of Law, DePaul University operates on a quarter system. The College of Law operates on the semester system. Classes in the Fall and Spring semesters are 16 weeks in length (including finals week) and it offers a Summer Session of 7 weeks (including final exams). Launched in 2012, WKU offers a unique model of higher education in partnership with Kean University, a comprehensive, public university in the state of New Jersey that is accredited by the Middle States Commission on Higher Education. WKU sits on approximately 500 beautiful acres and currently enrolls about 5,500 undergraduate and graduate students, and it is now in the midst of a rapid growth that will bring enrollment to 7,000 students within the next three years. All instruction is in English, and all curriculum is provided by Kean University. In addition to its current 18 undergraduate programs, WKU has been approved by the Ministry of Education for offering 14 Master s and 3 doctorate programs including the M.A. in Communication. WKU highly values research-powered teaching and learning, and the average number of faculty publications and the Field-weighted Citation Impact are among the best of leading Chinese academic institutions. Wenzhou is one of the most vibrant and economically advanced developed cities on China s East Coast, located one hour by plane and three hours by high-speed train from Shanghai Position: The College of Liberal Arts is seeking highly motivated individuals to join the Communication department at WKU. All faculty positions are full-time assignments, effective for the year of 2027 Spring or the 2027 Fall semester. These positions are full-time assignments appointed on a 3-year contract at the first instance and are renewable upon successful reappointment review. A tenure-track Assistant/Associate Professor is a full time, 10-month employee who teaches 24 credits per academic year. Tenure-track faculty normally teach 2 different courses with each section consisting typically of 25 students. Six credits of teaching release time will be provided to new faculty each year for the first three consecutive years of the appointment to support external research grant development and other significant research endeavors. Thereafter, release time may be available by application on competitive basis. A start-up grant (up to 80,000 RMB) will be provided to launch student-engaging research programs. Successful candidates will engage in high-quality teaching, impactful research, academic advising, student learning support, and service contributions to the university and the broader professional community. Tenure-track faculty must demonstrate a strong record of publication in reputable, peer-reviewed journals that are widely respected within the field. Teaching assignments and related responsibilities may include day, evening and weekend. Interest or experience in using advanced instructional technologies to improve the teaching/learning process is highly desirable. All faculty may be required to teach General Education courses as needed. Opportunities are also available to teach disciplinary support courses. Tenure-track candidates should possess a strong track record of publication and be ready to lead their research groups independently. Tenure-track candidates are expected to plan and conduct research and develop extramurally funded research programs involving students, which is essential for tenure and promotion. Tenure track candidates are also expected to publish peer-reviewed journal articles in impactful journals in Communication or closely related fields. jobs.detailText:
The University of St. Thomas (UST) announces a national search for the position of Dean of the Cameron School of Business, with employment to begin July 1, 2027. As UST works to increase enrollment and strengthen its standing as a major institution of higher education, we seek a Dean who will ensure the delivery of high-quality programs and instruction, foster mission-focused faculty development, and guide the strategic growth of the school while remaining faithful to the University's distinctive Catholic mission. UST prepares students for success in today's dynamic economy through a strong core curriculum in the liberal arts, exceptionally talented and dedicated faculty, and innovative co-curricular programs. An independent, coeducational private university, UST enrolls nearly 4,000 students (more than 3,000 undergraduates and almost 700 graduate students) from 34 states and 61 countries. We are Houston's only Catholic university, welcoming students of all faiths and backgrounds, and our student body reflects the city we serve. Houston is the nation's fourth-largest city and home to one of the most dynamic business environments in the world: a global center of energy, health care and life sciences, international trade, shipping and logistics, aerospace, and finance, with more than twenty Fortune 500 headquarters. The Cameron School of Business is located in the heart of this economy and is uniquely positioned to serve it. The Cameron School of Business offers undergraduate and graduate programs in business administration, management, marketing, accounting, finance, economics, and international business, including the Master of Business Administration (MBA) and a nationally recognized Master in Clinical Translation Management. The Dean's primary responsibility is stewardship of the school's academic performance and enrollment growth. The Dean will also serve as the school's principal ambassador to the Houston business community, cultivating partnerships with corporations, professional firms, entrepreneurs, alumni, and nonprofit organizations; ensuring that the school's programs and faculty scholarship respond to the needs of the region's employers; and maintaining the school's accreditations. The Dean reports directly to the Provost and serves as the chief academic and administrative officer of the Cameron School of Business. Stewardship and Strategic Role Functions Develop and lead a clear strategic vision for the Cameron School of Business, aligned with the University's strategic plan and Catholic mission, and integrate it into the school's academic planning and operations. Guide the strategic development, implementation, and evaluation of the school's academic programs to ensure their quality, relevance, and market competitiveness. Lead enrollment growth across the school, with particular emphasis on expanding the MBA program and other graduate offerings, by working closely with Enrollment Management and Marketing on recruitment strategy, program positioning, and yield. Ensure that the school's degree programs, concentrations, certificates, and executive education offerings are aligned with the workforce needs of the Houston and Gulf Coast business community, including energy, health care, finance, logistics, and technology, and lead the development of new programs where demand warrants. Foster the conditions and relationships that support creativity, innovation, and the formation of learning communities among faculty and students. Support faculty and staff professional development at both the individual and the departmental level. External Relations and Community Engagement Serve as the principal representative of the Cameron School of Business to the Houston business community, actively building and maintaining relationships with corporate executives, professional associations, chambers of commerce, and civic organizations. Lead a Dean's Business Advisory Council of regional executives to inform curriculum, provide internships and placement opportunities for students, and strengthen the school's reputation. Send job Job Details About Wenzhou-Kean University Wenzhou-Kean University (WKU), located in Wenzhou, China, one of three Sino-American universities along with NYU Shanghai and Duke Kunshan University, is approved by the Ministry of Education of China. Launched in 2012, WKU offers a unique model of higher education in partnership with Kean University, a comprehensive, public university in the state of New Jersey that is accredited by the Middle States Commission on Higher Education. WKU sits on approximately 500 beautiful acres and currently enrolls about 5,500 undergraduate and graduate students, and it is now in the midst of a rapid growth that will bring enrollment to 7,000 students within the next three years. All instruction is in English, and all curriculum is provided by Kean University. In addition to its current 18 undergraduate programs, WKU has been approved by the Ministry of Education for offering 14 Master s and 3 doctorate programs including the M.A. in Communication. WKU highly values research-powered teaching and learning, and the average number of faculty publications and the Field-weighted Citation Impact are among the best of leading Chinese academic institutions. Wenzhou is one of the most vibrant and economically advanced developed cities on China s East Coast, located one hour by plane and three hours by high-speed train from Shanghai. Position: The College of Liberal Arts is seeking highly motivated individuals to join the Communication department at WKU. All faculty positions are full-time assignments, effective for the year of 2027 Spring or the 2027 Fall semester. These positions are full-time assignments appointed on a 3-year contract at the first instance and are renewable upon successful reappointment review. A Lecturer is a full-time, 10-month employee who teaches 30 credits per year. Or a Lecturer is a full-time, 11-month employee who teaches 39 credits per year. A lecturer provides student and learning support services during the assigned period. Lecturers will be expected to provide high quality teaching, student advisement, learning support services, and service to the university/college/school/program and/or professional community; and perform related work as required. Lecturer positions are non-tenure track. Teaching assignments and related responsibilities may include day, evening and weekend. Interest or experience in using advanced instructional technologies to improve the teaching/learning process is highly desirable. All faculty may be required to teach General Education courses as needed. Opportunities are also available to teach disciplinary support courses. Qualifications: A Ph.D. in Communication Studies or related field is required; ABD can be considered with completion prior to the effective date of employment. English fluency is required. Candidates should be able to teach a full range of undergraduate and postgraduate Communication courses related to Digital Media and Storytelling, including but not limited to: Media and Film Production, Digital Storytelling, AI, Communication and Digital Technology, Organisational Theory & Culture, Research Methods in Communication, and other upper level Communication electives. A minimum of two years of teaching experience in a college or university setting is preferred. Candidates with doctorate degrees from reputable universities (Carnegie R1 institutions or comparable research institutions with strong academic reputation in the fields) are encouraged to apply. Faculty positions at WKU offer: Annual salary is commensurate with qualifications and experience with the range from USD $60,000-$70,000 for Lecturer. Salary of extraordinary candidates shall be determined on a case-by-case basis. A well-rounded healthcare coverage, housing options and subsidy up to $3,000, home traveling up to $6,000 (2 international round-trip airfares), a reimbursement to cover relocation expenses up to $1,000 and shuttle bus to campus for work. WKU tuition waiver up to 50% for spouse/dependent children of faculty for undergraduate programs. The opportunity to teach high-quality students. About 50% of graduates have been admitted to graduate schools at the World s Top 50 Universities, and about 60% of graduates at the World s Top 100 Universities. Application Information: Applicants are REQUIRED to apply online . To receive full consideration by the search committee, candidates need to submit the following documents via Interfolio( https://apply.interfolio.com/195449 ). Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until positions are filled. Candidates should send cover letter, CV, statement of teaching philosophy, a research statement describing research interests, past accomplishments in research (such as 2-3 most representative peer-reviewed academic publications), and future research plans, unofficial transcripts, and the email contact information of three professional references, including references/names of potential referees from a current or recent direct supervisor. Three current letters of recommendation (within the last 3 months) will be required before advancement. Official transcripts for all degrees are required before appointment. Background Screening: Wenzhou-Kean University conducts background screenings on all candidates upon acceptance of a contingent offer and may use a third-party administrator to conduct background screenings. Send job Job Details Organization Job Details Description Adjuncts are hired on a course basis each term. Salary Range for Adjuncts teaching in this academic area is $300.00 - $4,500.00 per course. Governors State University’s College of Health and Human Services seeks to create an available pool of Adjunct Clinical and Teaching Faculty candidates to supervise graduate students and teach undergraduate and graduate courses in the Communication Disorders program. The major responsibilities of an adjunct faculty member would include one or more of the following:1. to serve as university supervisor of graduate students in external practica in speech-language pathology (i.e., serve as liaison between university and external practicum site); 2. to serve as a clinical supervisor of graduate students in a pre-practicum course in speech-language in pediatric and adult community settings; 3. to teach undergraduate and/or graduate courses in areas of need including child language, adult language, voice, and/or fluency. At Governors State University, adjunct faculty are hired as temporary faculty with teaching responsibilities for a specific course in a semester or summer session. Adjuncts are not a part of the faculty bargaining unit and are not included in membership of the Faculty Senate. Interested individuals are invited to complete a faculty profile and submit a cover letter that indicates the position/s applied for, a curriculum vitae, and transcripts for consideration. Required and Preferred Qualifications Minimum Qualifications - Master’s Degree in Speech-Language Pathology.-Certificate of Clinical Competence in Speech-Language Pathology (CCC-SLP).Preferred Qualifications -2 years of post-CFY clinical experience as an SLP-Experience supervising graduate students in clinical settings in speech-language pathology-Teaching experience. Supplemental Information Please attach the following documents to your application: Cover Letter CV or Resume Transcript Organization Working at Governors State University Success by Degrees GSU is an “island of excellence,” according to Dr. Martha J. Kanter, Under Secretary of the United States Department of Education. With bold, new initiatives, 23 bachelor’s, 27 master’s, and five doctoral degree programs, GSU excels at providing the quality education that is essential for success in today’s world. Success by Opportunity GSU’s exemplary efforts bring unequalled education opportunities to the region’s diverse population. The university is remarkably inclusive and serves students from a wide range of socio-economic and cultural backgrounds. The student body, like the faculty and staff, reflect a rich blend of ideas, perspectives, talents, and life experiences. Success by Innovation GSU, expanding on its commitment to excellence and reflecting the best research on student success, will become a full-service university with the admission of its inaugural freshman class in 2014. The groundbreaking Dual Degree Program encourages community college students to complete both an associate and bachelor’s degree at an affordable tuition rate and with comprehensive academic advising. Success by Commitment GSU is committed to serving as the region’s public square and making the community stronger through programs and partnerships in education, healthcare, government, and business. The Center for Performing Arts and Nathan Manilow Sculpture Park integrate arts and education. The university is also fully committed to sustainability through its alternative energy and conservation efforts. Success by Excellence GSU, the only public university in the Chicago Southland region, is a national model in providing education pathways that lead its graduates to lives rich in purpose, commitment, and contribution. jobs.detailText: The University of St.Gallen and its School of Management are inviting applications for an Associate Professorship / Assistant Professorship with Tenure Track (Open Rank) in Technology and Innovation Management. The triple accredited (EQUIS, AACSB, AMBA) university offers a stimulating and well-equipped research environment with a large network ranging from start-ups, small businesses to large firms to engage in research. The new professorship in the School of Management will become part of our dynamic faculty and will be invited to join the Institute of Technology Management (ITEM-HSG) and the Global Center for Entrepreneurship and Innovation. We are seeking a colleague with proven expertise in one or more of the key domains of Technology and Innovation Management, including Global R&D, Innovation Strategy, Digital Innovation, Open Innovation, AI-driven Innovation, Technology Strategy, or related fields. Depending on qualifications, the appointment will be made at the level of Associate Professor or Assistant Professor with Tenure Track. The ideal candidate for the Associate Professorship has an internationally recognised and leading track record in research in leading journals in the field of Technology and Innovation Management, reflected in publications in top journals (e.g. FT50), a strong pipeline of promising research projects, a strong international academic network, ties with industry, and excellent teaching skills at all levels, including Executive Education. According to our claim "From insight to impact", the future colleague should convey scientific knowledge to students and have a significant impact on theory and practice. The successful candidate will also attract competitive external research funding (e.g. SNF, Innosuisse, ERC or industry collaborations), contribute actively to the academic community and governance of the University, and strengthen interdisciplinary collaboration across the School of Management and related technology-oriented disciplines. Associate Professors at the University of St.Gallen are provided with a budget to hire a doctoral student. The University of St.Gallen is committed to promoting equal opportunities and an inclusive working culture. We explicitly encourage women and members of underrepresented groups to apply. JJC offers regular full-time positions a variety of fringe benefits including retirement benefits, holidays, personal time, and other discounts/reimbursement for classes. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. The student population at the college is diverse in ethnicity, gender, language, age and background. Joliet Junior College is an AA/EO employer and strongly encourages applications from candidates who would enhance the diversity of its staff. POSITION SUMMARY A Community Education Instructor is an instructor hired for an individual seminar for which he/she is qualified. The Community Education Instructor reports to one of the following coordinators (Community Education/Training/Contract Training) and provides quality instruction for the assigned courses. The instructor works with full-time staff in assessing students and following all course guidelines. Willingness to provide instructions at other campus sites is required. ESSENTIAL JOB DUTIES AND KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 1. Provide instruction using appropriate technology, appropriate and effective standards of delivery, and a variety of methods of instruction. 2. To create a student-centered learning environment that is accessible to individual learners with diverse educational needs and goals. 3. Facilitate student learning by preparing, delivering, and assessing learning activities that are consistent with approved course outcomes. 4. Improve student learning by using a variety of teaching strategies. 5. Cultivate open-minded inquiry. 6. Encourage thoughtful, self-reflective assessment. 7. Promote cooperation and mutual respect among students. 8. Provide applicable and relevant classroom exercises. 9. Infuse multicultural and diverse perspectives into the instructional processes as appropriate, and conduct classes in a manner that demonstrates respect for individual and cultural differences. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS 1. One (1) year of experience in the subject matter. 2. Certification, licensure, endorsements and related experience will be considered. 3. Experience in instructional/classroom technology. 4. Demonstrated commitment to teaching and learning. 5. Ability to establish and maintain cooperative and effective working relationships with other members of the college and community, displaying cultural competence as well as emotional intelligence. 6. Demonstrated commitment to the college’s core values of respect and inclusion, sustainability, integrity, collaboration, humor and well-being, innovation, and quality. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 1. Associate’s Degree in Education, subject matter, or closely related field 2. Experience with traditional and non-traditional students from diverse backgrounds. 3. English and Spanish verbal and written communication proficiency. 4. Demonstrated multicultural competence. PHYSICAL DEMANDS 1. Normal classroom physical demands. WORKING CONDITIONS 1. Duties are performed indoors in the usual classroom and/or lab environment. BENEFITS Click on the link for information about JJC's Benefits: Part Time - Adjunct Faculty Full Time/Part Time: Part time Union (If Applicable): Scheduled Hours: 28 Organization Working at Joliet Junior College Joliet Junior College, the nation's first public community college, offers pre-baccalaureate programs for students planning to transfer to a four-year university. A comprehensive community college, JJC also provides occupational education leading directly to employment, adult education and literacy programs, workforce development services, and student support services. Tucked in the middle of a wildlife preserve, bridging the banks of a lake and surrounded by its own Arboretum, Joliet Junior College is an educational community that embraces diversity and promotes personal growth. Each year, more than 35,000 students find the diverse, comprehensive high quality educational experience they are looking for at JJC. We hope that you will take a few minutes to explore the job opportunities we have available and consider becoming a part of this experience. The recruitment of qualified and diverse personnel is the cornerstone of JJC's commitment to an innovative, collaborative and inclusive educational community. At JJC, we respect the wealth of knowledge and experience each of our employees brings to the workplace. The College supports this commitment by providing personnel with excellent terms and conditions of employment, outstanding health and welfare benefits and programs for a secure retirement. JJC employees work in a wide variety of roles within the college, including faculty, support staff, and administrative positions. With such a diverse range of professions, JJC ensures that a wealth of development opportunities is available to employees. From personal growth, career advancement, and a dynamic and rewarding work atmosphere, employees have the resources they need to achieve a successful and fulfilling career at JJC. Joliet Junior College's open search procedures allow us to find the best available candidates for positions and to provide a balanced workforce to reflect the ethnic composition of the District we serve. museums—the Kimbell Art Museum, the Modern Art Museum of Fort Worth
and the Amon Carter Museum of American Art. The Bass Performance
Hall is one of the premier performance venues in the country.
Concerts, film festivals and other events are held regularly at
Sundance Square, Panther Island and Near Southside venues. Required Application Materials & Application

All department faculty participate in the life of our campus community, including career fairs, faculty functions, recruiting sessions and other events. Located just 15 miles from Washington, D.C., we offer a broad undergraduate program with more than 300 majors; six minor programs; a vibrant MA program including strategic communication; health communication; science, environment, and risk communication; and media and culture specialties; and a highly ranked PhD program emphasizing health; strategic; and science, environment, and risk communication. The department also offers a graduate certificate in science communication. We serve a diverse population of undergraduate and graduate students who bring a wide variety of cultures and backgrounds to our classrooms. Additionally, the department supports several co-curricular activities, including debate, forensics, Public Relations Student Society of America (PRSSA), Society of Professional Journalists (SPJ), and a comprehensive student media program. The research life of the department includes both undergraduate and graduate research and is reflected in the activities and outreach of its faculty, including those of the Center for Climate Change Communication (4C); the Communication, Health, and Relational Media (CHARM) research lab; the Center for Health and Risk Communication (CHRC); the Pop Culture lab; and the Character Assassination and Reputation Politics (CARP) research lab, in addition to several university-wide research centers and institutes including the Institute for Digital Innovation. For more information on the Department of Communication at George Mason University, visit communication.gmu.edu . About the Position: The Department of Communication in the College of Humanities and Social Sciences at George Mason University seeks a full-time, tenure-track Assistant Professor of Communication, with a specialty in new/emerging communication technology and innovative research methods. Applicants should have a PhD in Communication or a closely related field. We welcome candidates from any communication subfield. We are especially interested in those whose work engages one or more of our core areas: strategic communication and public relations; health communication; science, environment, and risk communication; media studies; journalism; or advocacy and political communication. The successful candidate will demonstrate an active research agenda focused on new/emerging communication technologies with innovative research methods, a record of competitive conference papers and/or scholarly publications commensurate with experience, an ongoing research agenda, a commitment to excellence in teaching and mentoring a diverse student body, and a willingness to contribute to departmental and university service. We welcome all methodological approaches and specifically seek a candidate who pursues innovative methods to examine and/or utilize new and emerging technology. Candidates should demonstrate an ability to teach graduate and undergraduate courses in a variety of areas, as listed above. Overall, teaching experience at the university level is preferred. professional experience in digital media production, including
studio production, cinematography, and video editing; knowledge of

cameras required; proficiency in operating multicamera video
switchers for live or recorded broadcasts. Two years teaching
and/or training in the field preferred; experience preferably at
the college level. Academic transcripts must be submitted with
application. Class Specific Essential Duties Faculty teach 15 credits per semester, hold 5 office hours per
week, serve the college through committees and/or other service,

professional development. CCBC is committed to equal opportunity
and seek faculty who demonstrate the ability to function
effectively within a diverse population. We invite candidates to
apply who will work with us to continually improve the CCBC student
experience. jobs.detailText: About ZIBS Rooted in China with a global vision, Zhejiang University International Business School (ZIBS) uphold s its "5i" philos ophy— International, Interdisciplinary, Innovative, Inclusive and Integrative. The School promotes exchange and mutual understanding across global business communities, facilitates the deep integration of technological innovation and industry, and strives to nurture top‑tier interdisciplinary innovators equipped with global leadership capabilities. ZIBS pursues targeted, distinctive development in emerging interdisciplinary areas including Sci‑Tech Finance, Digital Intelligence Management, and International Business and Globalization. Adhering to a strategy of selectivity, excellence and specialization, ZIBS has built high‑level research platforms. Drawing on these resources, the school aims to develop a global‑minded international business education model centered on science and technology. Preferred Research Areas Corporate Finance, FinTech, Quantitative Finance, Digital Accounting, Digital Marketing, Information Systems and Business Analytics, International Business, Organizations and Strategy in the Digital Age, as well as related areas. Positions Full Professor: Well‑known scholars, academicians and highly‑cited researchers in their respective fields, with extensive teaching and research experience and the capacity to lead disciplinary development. Associate Professor (Tenured or Tenure-Track): Assistant professor or above at world renowned universities, strong candidates of national young talent programs. Demonstrate strong academic influence, with the ability of leading high-quality research projects. Assistant Professor (Tenure-Track): Young talents with demonstrated academic potential and competitiveness for national‑level young talent programs, with an outstanding publication record or strong potential to publish in top‑tier journals. Haina Scholar (Teaching-Track) : This full-time teaching-track position is primarily open to Non-Chinese candidates. Applicants should possess a solid theoretical foundation and professional expertise, with the ability to conduct high-quality research and teaching. A doctoral degree from a reputable university worldwide and at least two years of research and teaching experience are generally required. Postdoctoral Fellow PhD graduates from world-renowned universities with strong potential for excellent research and teaching performance. Work and Living Conditions 1. Academic environment: Drawing on Zhejiang University’s premier academic standing, the school provides an open, inclusive research climate and world‑class international educational resources, nurtured by a collegial and diverse international faculty body. 2. Career Development: Independent PI role with doctoral supervision privileges (available to tenure-track and tenured faculty); Well-defined career progression with annual reviews; access to professional development training. 3. Research support: Start-up fund will be commensurate in line with qualifications, plus strong support for allocation of doctor/master students and postdoctoral recruitment quota. A bilingual campus with international efficient administrative and service structure. 4. Remuneration and benefits: Competitive remuneration commensurate with qualifications and experience. 5. Housing arrangement: Rental of a fully furnished apartment (available to all faculty); purchase of an on-campus Hainashire apartment (available for tenure-track and tenured positions). 6. Other support: Enrollment of children in preferred local schools; Assist in permanent residence permit application for foreign faculty; Fine medical services provided by the two branch sections of the affiliated hospitals of ZJU in the neighborhood, etc. Application All applicants shall provide the following application materials (in PDF format) to [email protected] , with the subject titled “Name - Position Applied For”. Please also specify in application email the source platform through which you learned about this vacancy. 1. A detailed CV (please include your current email address, attached with a recent color ID photo or provide the photo separately); 2. A cover letter; 3. A research statement; 4. A teaching statement; 5. Three recommendation letters; 6. Three representative publications or other innovative research achievements (for papers accepted or in the R&R stage ， please provide supporting documents) ； 7. Identification documents (non-Mainland China residents can provide passports or other identification documents); 8. Educational and degree certificates; * To receive full consideration, applications should be received online by November 10, 2026, but the search will remain open until filled. Qualified applicants will usually receive an email notification within 1–2 weeks after submission; otherwise, it will be assumed that they did not pass the initial screening. jobs.detailText: Position Description NYU Shanghai is currently inviting applications for a faculty position in Management and Organizations at all ranks. For further details about the research centers and institutes at NYU Shanghai, please visit this webpage: https://research.shanghai.nyu.edu/. Terms of employment at NYU Shanghai are comparable to NYU New York and other U.S. institutions with respect to research start-up funds and compensation, and they include housing subsidies and educational subsidies for children. Faculty may in certain cases have the opportunity to spend time at NYU New York and other sites of the NYU Global Network, engaging in both research and teaching. Qualifications We seek candidates who have completed a Ph.D. in Management and Organizations or a closely related discipline. We invite applications from candidates in any field and have a special interest in those with expertise in Organizational Theory, Strategy, and Entrepreneurship. Application Instructions Applicants should submit a cover letter, curriculum vitae, statement of research, statement of teaching interests, and at least one writing sample (e.g., job market paper) via Interfolio. Additionally, applicants (applying at the Assistant or Associate without tenure ranks) will be prompted to enter the names and email addresses of at least three evaluators. Each referee will be contacted to upload a confidential letter of recommendation through Interfolio. Applications may be received until October 31st, 2026. Review of applications will begin on October 15th, 2026 and will continue until the position is filled. To apply, follow this link: https://apply.interfolio.com/194865. If you have any questions, please email the NYU Shanghai NY Office of Faculty Recruitment: [email protected] . About NYU Shanghai NYU Shanghai is the third degree-granting campus within New York University’s Global Network. It is the first higher education joint venture in China authorized to grant degrees that are accredited in the U.S. as well as in China. All teaching is conducted in English. A research university with liberal arts and science at its core, NYU Shanghai resides in one of the world's great cities with a vibrant intellectual community. NYU Shanghai recruits scholars of the highest caliber who are committed to NYU's global vision of transformative teaching and innovative research and who embody the global society in which we live. NYU’s Global Network includes degree-granting campuses in New York, Shanghai, and Abu Dhabi, complemented by thirteen additional academic centers across the world. Faculty and students may circulate within the Network in pursuit of common research interests and cross-cultural, interdisciplinary endeavors, both local and global. For people in the EU, click here for information on your privacy rights under GDPR: www.nyu.edu/it/gdpr. Send job Job Details The Texas A&M University College of Performance, Visualization & Fine Arts (PVFA) invites applications for a full-time, nine-month tenure-track or a tenured faculty position in Interactive Media and Creative Technology at the rank of Assistant Professor or Associate Professor. Rank and tenure status will be commensurate with the candidate’s academic and professional experience and qualifications. The anticipated start date is August 1, 2027. The College and the Technical Arts & Interactive Media (TAIM) Section in the Visualization Program seek an innovative scholar, artist, designer, and educator whose research and creative practice advance the evolving fields of interactive art and design, computational media, and interdisciplinary creative technologies. We are particularly interested in candidates whose work investigates how emerging technologies can expand creative expression, human experience, and design innovation through artistic inquiry, experimentation, critical engagement, and technological exploration. The successful candidate will join a vibrant interdisciplinary environment that bridges art, design, computation, science, and technology. They will be expected to establish and sustain a nationally and internationally recognized program of scholarly and/or creative research and contribute to teaching and mentorship across the Visualization Program’s undergraduate, master’s, and PhD programs. We value collaborative and forward-looking research and creative practices that address contemporary opportunities and challenges through innovative approaches to interactive systems, creative computation, emerging media, and human-centered technologies. Candidates should demonstrate the potential for, or an established record of, scholarly and creative excellence and the capacity to develop a significant and visible research and/or creative practice appropriate to their career stage. We especially welcome work that integrates artistic practice, design research, computational approaches, and technological innovation through interdisciplinary methods. Areas of expertise may include, but are not limited to: · Interactive Art and Design · Creative Technologies · Computational Media and Creative Coding · Immersive and Spatial Media (AR/VR/MR/XR) · Human-Computer Interaction and Human-AI Interaction Design · Artificial Intelligence and Creative Practice · Physical Computing and Responsive Environments · Generative and Procedural Art · Computational Storytelling and Interactive Narrative · Media Arts and Experimental Interfaces · Digital Performance and Performative Technologies · Other emerging interdisciplinary areas at the intersection of art, design, computation, science, and technology The ideal candidate will demonstrate a commitment to interdisciplinary research, creative practice, teaching, and mentorship and will contribute to the Technical Arts & Interactive Media Section’s mission of integrating artistic creativity, scientific inquiry, design thinking, and technological innovation. Through research, creative activity, teaching, and collaboration, the successful candidate will help shape new directions for visual and interactive experiences and contribute to the continued development of the Visualization Program’s undergraduate and graduate educational and research initiatives. Send job Job Details The Department of Journalism and Media Studies at Rutgers University’s School of Communication and Information invites applications for an advanced Associate or Full Professor position in the area of Media Industries. We define media industries broadly, including news, music, technology, fashion, sports, and popular culture. The expected start date is September 1, 2027. Some examples of (but not limited to) the types of scholarship that would fit the call include : Social, political and/or cultural implications for media of artificial intelligence Critical approaches to media and data infrastructures, platforms, and algorithms Creator economies (advocacy, activism, professionalization, uneven access) Political economy of emerging media Cultural policies and legislation (regulation, ethical issues, and intellectual property) Intersection of media industries with environmental issues and vulnerable populations Geopolitics and global media corporations Changes in social media, streaming, and/or immersive platforms Evolutions in the news industry and journalistic practices Media industries and audiences Media production hubs and urban transformations Promotion, media strategy, and social change Media labor dynamics We are especially interested in scholars who study media industries in relation to power and inequality, particularly in the context of, but not limited to, gender/queer/disability studies. Having or building a network of industry/institutional connections is a plus. Job Responsibilities Responsibilities of tenured faculty members include undergraduate and graduate teaching assignments, an active program of research in the candidate’s area of scholarly expertise, and service contributions in accordance with the university policy for tenured appointments. We are seeking someone with leadership experience and/or interest in eventual departmental leadership. Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey, is among America’s highest-ranked, most diverse public research universities and is the oldest, largest, and top-ranked public university in the New York/New Jersey metropolitan area. Established in 1766 and the state’s land-grant institution, Rutgers is home to more than 71,000 students and 27,300 full- and part-time faculty and staff who learn, work, and serve the public at three main Rutgers campuses across New Jersey and at locations around the region. With 29 schools and colleges, over 550 degree programs, over 610,000 alumni, and thousands of professional and personal enrichment continuing education programs, Rutgers’ impact is felt around the world. For more information see www.rutgers.edu. The School of Communication and Information (SC&I) on the Rutgers-New Brunswick campus houses a dynamic community of scholars who conduct research and teach in the areas of communication, information science, media studies, information technology, journalism, librarianship, organizational and health communication, public relations, and other professional practice areas. SC&I has more than 2,500 matriculating students and teaches thousands of other Rutgers students in our five undergraduate programs, two masters degrees, interdisciplinary doctoral program, and non-degree continuing education programs. We value our culture of collegiality and we work hard to support the success of our full- and part-time faculty, staff, and students. For more about the school and its activities, see: http://comminfo.rutgers.edu. Faculty in the Department of Journalism and Media Studies have doctoral and professional degrees in a variety of fields, including communication, journalism, law, sociology, history, anthropology and other areas. We study and practice the operation of media at local, national, and international levels, and our research methods range from humanistic to social scientific. This year marks the 100-year anniversary of journalism education at Rutgers. For more about the department, see: https://sci.rutgers.edu/departments/journalism-and-media-studies-department Rutgers University is an AA/EEO employer - M/F/Veteran/Disability. For additional information please see our Non-Discrimination Statement. jobs.detailText: Tenure-Track Assistant Professor – Leading People and Organizations Gabelli School of Business, Fordham University The Leading People and Organizations (LPO) Area at the Gabelli School of Business invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track faculty position at the rank of Assistant Professor, beginning Fall 2027. We welcome applicants whose research addresses questions at the intersection of organizations and society, with particular interest in the following areas: organizational theory and design, sustainability and social impact, entrepreneurship and innovation, and the management of artificial intelligence and emerging technologies. Candidates whose work engages questions of purpose, responsibility, and human flourishing in organizational life are especially encouraged to apply. The LPO Area is built around a conviction that management scholarship should advance human dignity and well-being — not merely organizational efficiency. Our faculty study how individuals, teams, and organizations can be forces for good: through ethical leadership, trustworthy institutions, social innovation, and sustainable enterprise. The LPO Area is home to the Center for Humanistic Management and Fordham's sustainable business, management, and entrepreneurship programs, including the Fordham Foundry. Faculty engage with both scholarly communities and the broader New York City business ecosystem across Fordham's Lincoln Center and Rose Hill campuses. The ideal candidate must possess a Ph.D. in Management, Organizational Behavior, or a related field from an accredited institution (expected completion no later than July 1, 2027, is acceptable). Candidates must demonstrate strong research potential and commitment to excellence in graduate and undergraduate teaching. We are a collaborative area that values intellectual generosity, and we seek colleagues who thrive in an environment of mutual support and shared purpose. Applications should include a cover letter providing a research statement and description of teaching interests, a curriculum vitae, three letters of reference, and an example of scholarly work. All materials should be submitted via Interfolio at Apply - Interfolio by September 1, 2026 . Candidates are encouraged to apply early, as interview decisions may be made before the deadline. Questions may be directed to Randy Krevat at [email protected] . Fordham University is an independent Catholic university in the Jesuit tradition. Fordham's Jesuit mission emphasizes ethical leadership, social responsibility, and engagement with the broader public good, values that animate the LPO faculty's teaching and scholarship. Fordham's Gabelli School of Business is guided by the principle of "Business with Purpose" — preparing leaders who generate not only profit, but wide-ranging benefits for society. The Gabelli School of Business is AACSB-accredited. Fordham is an Equal Opportunity Employer and welcomes applications from candidates of all backgrounds.

jobs.snippet: Call for Applications At the University of St.Gallen, Switzerland, researchers from different disciplines and generations convene at St.Gallen Collegium. jobs.detailText:
Call for Applications At the University of St.Gallen, Switzerland, researchers from different disciplines and generations convene at St.Gallen Collegium. Fellows pursue their own research and a joint project focusing on a theme related to one of the Grand Challenges of our time. For the third Collegium year 2027/2028 (September 1, 2027-May 31, 2028), St.Gallen Collegium will award fellowships to scholars whose work addresses the theme: "Performance: The What, How, and Why of Optimization" About the Theme The call for “more performance” has returned with force across European business and politics as a reaction to perceived decreasing productivity of many economies. It simultaneously reflects changing values and preferences of their societies as to what, how, and why shall be optimized. Companies announce this openly: Nestlé declares it wants to be more performance-driven; UBS insists that performance must again be at the center. Politics has followed suit. The Schweizerischer Arbeitgeberverband warns of a spreading culture of Lifestyle Freizeit. The German CDU campaigns on Leistung muss sich wieder lohnen — performance must pay. Commentators demand “work instead of woke.” The word does considerable heavy lifting. The concept itself is rarely examined. Performance, as we use it today, has a relatively recent history. The historian Nina Verheyen has argued that measurable, comparable individual performance took its current shape in the nineteenth century, shaped by the rise of mass schooling, industrial labor, and the welfare state. Earlier traditions tied performance more closely to the work itself — to craft, to care, to standards of excellence carried out within a practice and judged by its own internal norms. The shift towards abstracted, quantified output was not inevitable. It was constructed, and it can be interrogated. Much of what gets called individual performance has irreducibly relational features. Contributions emerge between people, in context, supported by predecessors, colleagues, institutions, and inherited knowledge. Measurement systems do not simply reflect performance — they constitute what counts as performance and render other kinds of contribution invisible. The colleague who unblocks others, the institutional memory carried by long-serving staff, the care work that makes everything else possible: these tend to fall outside what is captured and rewarded. The map is not the territory, but in performance cultures, the map increasingly determines whose work counts. The language of performance also carries significant moral weight. A meritocratic reading treats outcomes as broadly deserved and shortfalls as broadly personal. Harvard moral philosopher Michael Sandel has argued that this framing generates hubris among those who succeed and humiliation among those who do not — with consequences for social solidarity that extend well beyond the individuals concerned. Whether and how strongly this dynamic operates across different institutional and cultural settings is itself a pressing research question, one that has gained new urgency in recent debates on polarization, resentment, and the fraying of social cohesion. The performance of an economy is also shaped by forces no individual or firm controls. Demographic change is perhaps the most consequential of these. What does prosperity mean if, by 2050, approximately 30% of the Swiss population is over 65, compared to just 9% in 1950? What does it mean for productivity, innovation, and care if Germany's population begins to shrink and declines by an estimated 13% by mid-century? How can societies harness the potential of longer lives rather than treating extended longevity solely as a fiscal burden? These questions demand that we rethink how and what counts as economic performance — and for whom. The question of who defines what counts as performance, and who benefits from the categories thereby created, is partly political and philosophical, not only technical. St.Gallen Collegium invites researchers from all fields who are interested in a solution-oriented, interdisciplinary discourse on performance. Possible avenues of research include: – The history and gen
[Application instructions later in posting]
holars of any field; Associate Professors/Readers, Full Professors, emeriti/emeritae, as well as independent scholars are welcome to apply. 2 Junior Fellowships for young scholars from the global south: two fellowships are designated for advanced doctoral students or early postdoctoral scholars who are currently working at a university in the global south, preferably at an African university. Hans Christoph Binswanger Fellowship for a post-doctoral scholar: see separate application procedure. https://www.unisg.ch/en/research/research-at-hsg/prizes-and-awards/hans-christoph-binswanger-fellowship-and-prize/ Outreach Fellowship: Each year, an outreach fellow joins St.Gallen Collegium and works with the research fellows in the context of the joint project. The outreach fellow is part of the collaborative process and simultaneously a bridgebuilder who makes the work and findings of the Collegium more accessible to a broader audience. College of New Jersey (TCNJ) invites applications for a
tenure-track Assistant Professor position in technology-mediated
interpersonal communication. We seek an outstanding teacher-scholar
whose research and teaching expertise centers on the intersection
of interpersonal or relational communication and
technology-mediated communication. The successful candidate's research program should keep
interpersonal or relational communication at its core, even as it
engages with technology. Examples of research programs that align

communication processes such as conflict management,
self-disclosure, and social support unfold through
technology-mediated channels; and how technology-mediated
communication is used within, or influences, couples and families.

technology in society that does not also engage relational or
interpersonal communication falls outside the scope of this
search. Consistent with TCNJ's teacher-scholar model, the successful
candidate will teach undergraduate courses including Introduction

Methods, along with technology-mediated interpersonal communication
courses that reflect their research expertise, while developing
curriculum that bridges theory and practice. They will also mentor
undergraduate students in professional development and research. In

Communication Technologies, Health Communication, Interpersonal and

jobs.snippet: « A place where knowledge is created » – As a leading business university we set global standards for research and teaching by promoting integrative thought, responsible action and an entrepreneurial spirit of innovation in business and society. Associate Professorship / Assistant Professorship with Tenure Track (Open Rank) in Technology and Innovation Management The University of St.Gallen and it
jobs.detailText: « A place where knowledge is created » – As a leading business university we set global standards for research and teaching by promoting integrative thought, responsible action and an entrepreneurial spirit of innovation in business and society. Associate Professorship / Assistant Professorship with Tenure Track (Open Rank) in Technology and Innovation Management The University of St.Gallen and its School of Management are inviting applications for an Associate Professorship / Assistant Professorship with Tenure Track (Open Rank) in Technology and Innovation Management. The triple accredited (EQUIS, AACSB, AMBA) university offers a stimulating and well-equipped research environment with a large network ranging from start-ups, small businesses to large firms to engage in research. The new professorship in the School of Management will become part of our dynamic faculty and will be invited to join the Institute of Technology Management (ITEM-HSG) and the Global Center for Entrepreneurship and Innovation. We are seeking a colleague with proven expertise in one or more of the key domains of Technology and Innovation Management, including Global R&D, Innovation Strategy, Digital Innovation, Open Innovation, AI-driven Innovation, Technology Strategy, or related fields. Depending on qualifications, the appointment will be made at the level of Associate Professor or Assistant Professor with Tenure Track. The ideal candidate for the Associate Professorship has an internationally recognised and leading track record in research in leading journals in the field of Technology and Innovation Management, reflected in publications in top journals (e.g. FT50), a strong pipeline of promising research projects, a strong international academic network, ties with industry, and excellent teaching skills at all levels, including Executive Education. According to our claim "From insight to impact", the future colleague should convey scientific knowledge to students and have a significant impact on theory and practice. The successful candidate will also attract competitive external research funding (e.g. SNF, Innosuisse, ERC or industry collaborations), contribute actively to the academic community and governance of the University, and strengthen interdisciplinary collaboration across the School of Management and related technology-oriented disciplines. Associate Professors at the University of St.Gallen are provided with a budget to hire a doctoral student. The University of St.Gallen is committed to promoting equal opportunities and an inclusive working culture. We explicitly encourage women and members of underrepresented groups to apply. We offer dual-career and welcome services for newly appointed faculty (and their families). We seek to fill the position as of 1 August 2027 or by mutual agreement. For further information, please contact Professor Dr Bj ö rn Ambos, Dean of the School of Management and Chairman of the Appointment Committee ( [email protected] ). The application should include a cover letter, curriculum vitae, research and teaching statements (max. one page each), list of publications, teaching evaluations, two publications or working papers that best represent the applicant's current research, and contact information for two professional references that we may contact if shortlisted for the position. Candidates should submit their application to the President of the University of St.Gallen, Professor Dr Manuel Ammann, online via www.unisg.ch/professorships at the latest by 15 November 2026. Research talks are expected to take place on 20 January 2027.

Send job Job Details Organization Job Details Associate/ Full Professor of Interactive Media Film and Media Arts, School of Communication, American University The School of Communication at American University (AU) in Washington, D.C., invites applications for a full-time, faculty position at the rank of associate or full professor, with an emphasis on interactive storytelling, worldbuilding, and/or playful design in the public interest. Depending on qualifications, the appointee may be recommended for tenure at the time of hiring. Candidates should hold a terminal degree as appropriate to their focus, such as an MFA or Ph.D. The salary range is from $105,000- $124,000. The School of Communication (SOC) at American University engages the most pressing issues of our time through teaching, scholarship, and professional experiences in communication and media. In the Film and Media Arts division, our faculty and students make media that matters in and beyond one of the most dynamic and influential cities in the world. The candidate is expected to work closely with or lead American University’s Game & Interactive Media Center, which is a world-class hub for experiential education, interactive storytelling, and computational media with a public purpose. While the Center is increasingly focused on undergraduate learning, its graduate programs were ranked #24 in the world by the Princeton Review in 2026, including the MA in Game Design and the MFA in Games and Interactive Media. The Center recently launched a new minor in Game Design, with one track for media studies students and another for those with an interest in computer science and game development. The ideal candidate will be an outstanding media maker, educator, and curricular strategist. They should ideally be comfortable with many principles of good game design. The candidate’s practice in interactive media should connect to one or more domains in the public interest: the environment, health, urban and spatial planning, education, or social issue storytelling, and should interface with science communication and journalism, museums, nonprofits, etc. As more AI tools are integrated into production pipelines, the candidate should have some knowledge of where such tools are useful and how they can be guided, and be able to engage thoughtfully with students who are both AI resistant and AI enthusiasts. Job responsibilities may include teaching courses; directing undergraduate and graduate game programs; mentoring students; securing new partnerships and funding for original media projects and high-impact collaborations; and participating in School of Communication and University governance. The position, which will begin in August of 2027, comes with powerful opportunities for collaboration with a tremendous mix of organizations in Washington, DC, from arts funders to policy think tanks to global nonprofits. Collaborating across the university with our world-class faculty is particularly well-suited to the Game & Interactive Media Center and is encouraged. Consideration of applications will commence on November 1, 2026. Candidate interviews will begin in late 2026/early 2027 and continue until the position is filled. To apply, submit a letter of application, curriculum vitae, one letter of recommendation (two more letters will be requested for those who reach the interview stage), a teaching portfolio, optional creative portfolio, and optional excerpt of exemplary publications; finalist candidates will be asked for two letters of recommendation (likely to coincide with interviews). Send job Job Details The Chinese University of Hong Kong Applications are invited for:- School of Journalism and Communication Associate / Assistant Professor (Corporate Communication) (Ref: 260001NP) The School is seeking outstanding candidates, early career or established social scientists, with expertise in public relations and corporate communication in a digital and global society. Areas of particular interest include organizational responsibility and advocacy, government, public affairs, public-sector communication, digital engagement, and the ethical and governance implications of artificial intelligence and emerging technologies within this domain. The School also welcomes expertise that brings international, cross-cultural, or comparative perspectives to the field in a digital society. The appointee is expected to contribute to the teaching of the School's undergraduate and postgraduate programmes. The School welcomes candidates using qualitative, quantitative, or mixed methods approaches, and a variety of theoretical orientations. Applicants should have (i) a PhD in Communication or other related fields; (ii) a strong commitment to excellence in teaching and research; and (iii) demonstrated potential/ ability for research and a cohesive research agenda. Applicants capable of engaging in interdisciplinary research and collaboration are preferred. A highly competitive salary commensurate with qualifications will be offered. The comprehensive benefit package provided by the University includes generous academic leave, annual leave, medical care, retirement scheme contributions, contract-end gratuity, and housing benefits. Appointment will normally be made on contract basis for up to three years initially commencing August 2027, which, subject to mutual agreement, may lead to longer-term appointment or substantiation later. The School of Journalism and Communication has a strong focus on research and provides its members with solid support for their research work. Faculty members are productive and committed researchers as well as devoted educators. The faculty team at the School features a combination of highly promising young scholars and established scholars who are leaders in their own fields, including two elected Fellows of the International Communication Association. The School is ranked #16 globally in communication and media studies by the QS World University Ranking by Subject in 2026. The School has a strong tradition of upholding freedom of the press, of expression, and of academic research. Application Procedure To apply for the post, please complete the online application at http://career.cuhk.edu.hk/ and attach a letter of interest and CV. Review of applications and shortlisting will start in November until the post is filled. The University only accepts and considers applications submitted online for the post above via the CUHK career site. For more information and to apply online, please visit http://career.cuhk.edu.hk. jobs.detailText: Tenure-Track Faculty Position in Management All ranks ( Assistant , Associate , or Full Professor ). Beginning Fall 2027. SKK GSB invites applications for one or more tenure-track faculty position s in Management, at any rank, with the appointment beginning in Fall 2027. SKK GSB is home to a leading global MBA program in Korea , in the heart of Seoul, with an internationally recruited faculty and full-time MBA students from more than 25 countries. All instruction is in English; knowledge of Korean is not required. THE POSITION We welcome applications in all areas of m anagement , micro and macro. Candidates must hold a doctoral degree in management or a related field prior to appointment. We seek colleagues with a strong record of, or clear trajectory toward, publication in the top-tier journals in the field. Research excellence is the primary criterion for this appointment. We also care deeply about teaching, as our MBA programs are at the heart of the school, and we are looking for a colleague who will be an engaging and committed educator in the classroom. Across its programs, SKK GSB is building distinctive strength at the intersection of technology and management, including through its AI MBA program and its developing AI and Business Innovation Lab (AIBIL). jobs.detailText: Founded in 1850, the University of Rochester is one of the nation's leading research institutions and one of the top universities in the world for entrepreneurs. It is a member of the Association of American Universities and ranked 49th by U.S. News & World Report (2027) among national universities and 127th globally by Times of Higher Education . University faculty, scholars, artists, alumni, and students have revolutionized their fields, discovering ways to address the world's biggest challenges, earning notable recognitions including Nobel Prizes, Pulitzer Prizes, Grammy Awards, and Guggenheim and MacArthur Fellowships. The University's diverse community includes more than 3,900 full and part-time faculty members and nearly 12,000 students. Founded in 1958, Simon Business School offers undergraduate, MBA, specialized master’s, executive, online, and doctoral education. Its academic identity is grounded in an economics-based, analytical approach to business and a longstanding commitment to rigorous research. Simon develops analytical and adaptive problem-solvers who lead ideas and industries forward. The School’s top-ranked programs combine quantitative depth with strategic responsiveness, preparing graduates to turn insight into value-driving action. With deep connections across sectors, its global community is transforming the future of business. Simon today offers a broad portfolio of business education spanning the undergraduate through doctoral levels. Its graduate offerings include the Full-Time, Professional, and Executive MBA programs; specialized MS programs in Accountancy, Artificial Intelligence in Business, Business Analytics, Finance, Management, and Marketing Analytics; an MS in Medical Management; online programs; a PhD program and a Doctor of Business Administration. Simon recently forged partnerships with six colleges and universities, enabling students to earn a master’s degree in business in just one year after completing their undergraduate studies through the 4+1 Business Master’s Pathway program. Simon is intentionally small and highly personalized. The Full-Time MBA class entering in fall 2026 numbered 84 students representing 21 countries, with an average of five years of professional experience. The School’s specialized master’s programs add a substantial and globally diverse student population. Simon’s alumni community numbers approximately 19,000 and includes senior leaders in business and industry around the world. The School is entering an important new chapter with undergraduate business education now housed within Simon, thereby creating an opportunity to build a more integrated continuum of undergraduate and graduate business education and to deepen connections across the University of Rochester. Simon is particularly well positioned to leverage the University’s strengths in medicine and health care, engineering, data science and AI, entrepreneurship, the arts, and the growing innovation economy of Rochester and Western New York. Research is deeply embedded in Simon’s history and culture. The School has made important contributions to the fields of finance, accounting, economics, marketing, and organizational decision-making, and its faculty continue to produce influential scholarship across business disciplines. Three leading academic journals — the Journal of Financial Economics , Journal of Accounting & Economics , and Journal of Monetary Economics — were founded at the University of Rochester, reflecting the institution’s longstanding influence on modern economic and financial thought. Simon combines the resources and intellectual ambition of a leading research university with the intimacy of a relatively small business school. Its close-knit community, accessible faculty, highly engaged alumni, and longstanding international orientation have been defining features of the Simon experience. As the School looks to its future, it does so from a position of distinctive academic strength and with an opportunity to reimagine how that heritage can serve the rapidly changing needs of students, employers, and the business sector. Current rankings and outcomes include the following: #26 among U.S. business schools --- Bloomberg Businessweek , 2026 #34 among U.S. business schools — S. News & World Report , 2026 #29 among U.S. business schools — Financial Times , 2026 #2 in the U.S. for salary growth — Financial Times , 2026 #6 for ROI among top-35 U.S. business schools — Bloomberg Businessweek , 2025 #21 among US business schools and #37 globally in Linked In’s 2026 Top MBA Programs URochester is ranked #49 in US News and World Report for 2026 88% of job-seeking Full-Time MBA Class of 2025 graduates accepted employment within three months of graduation $162K average starting compensation for the Full-Time MBA Class of 2025 The Simon Business School Dean reports to the Provost and Chief Academic Officer and is a member of the University Deans’ Council and the President’s University Cabinet. The next Dean will have the opportunity to lead Simon’s next chapter, inheriting a distinguished research legacy, a strong faculty, an engaged alumni community, an expanded undergraduate mandate, and an opportunity to define a differentiated model for business education at a time of profound change in both higher education and the global economy. Academic candidates will be expected to hold credentials for appointment at the level of full professor. Nontraditional candidates should demonstrate a high level of professional success and a deep appreciation of the academic research mission. Nominations, inquiries, and expressions of interest should be sent to: [email protected] . At the University of Rochester, we are committed to fostering, cultivating, and preserving an inclusive and welcoming culture and are united by a strong commitment to be ever better—Meliora. It is an ideal that informs our shared mission to ensure all members of our community feel safe, respected, included, and valued. The base salary range for this position is $700,000 to $950,000 with final determination of compensation made after consideration of qualifications and experience.
