jobs.detailText: The Dispute Resolution Research Center at the Kellogg School of Management, Northwestern University, is seeking applicants for our notable postdoctoral fellowship. The primary criterion for acceptance is research excellence relevant to conflict or cooperation, broadly defined. The position is slated to start in September of 2027 and last for approximately three years. Salary is competitive, and the position will have access to research funding, including for independent projects. Applicants must have completed a PhD in a social science discipline (e.g., organizational behavior, sociology, psychology, economics) — or in a related discipline that can inform the social sciences (e.g., a “big data” discipline) — prior to the beginning of the fellowship. The fellow will conduct original research with one or more faculty members at Kellogg. Learn about our current and past postdoctoral fellows here . As the DRRC works closely with faculty in the Management and Organizations (MORS) department, applicants are encouraged to identify one or more MORS faculty members with whom they would be interested in collaborating. The fellow is expected to become actively involved in MORS and DRRC intellectual communities by regularly participating in colloquia, workshops and research seminars. The fellow is also welcome to audit PhD courses. For full consideration, please submit application materials by Sunday, November 15, 2026. You will need to submit: (1) a cover letter identifying at least one faculty member with whom you would be interested in collaborating (2) a current CV (3) a research statement that makes clear how your work is relevant to conflict or cooperation (4) up to two publications or manuscripts (5) the names and contact information for 2–3 people who will submit recommendation letters on your behalf Click here to apply. Northwestern University is an equal opportunity employer. Hiring is contingent upon eligibility to work in the United States.

statuses: Job Description: The Department of Communication at Villanova University seeks applicants for a tenure-track position in Computational Communication at the rank of Assistant Professor to begin Fall 2027. Successful applicants will have a terminal degree in Communication (Ph.D.), or allied discipline. ABD will be considered with degree completion by August 2027. They should demonstrate an active, theoretically grounded research agenda utilizing quantitative computational social science and big data analytics to investigate human communication processes, media ecosystems, and/or message dynamics. Applicants must possess demonstrated technical expertise in one or more of the following areas: Computational Text Analysis & NLP in Communication; Network Science & Digital-Trace Communication Data; Algorithmic & Machine Learning Approaches; Human-AI & Algorithmic Interaction; Emerging Computational Methods: Other advanced data science, artificial intelligence, or quantitative methodologies applied to communication phenomena not listed above. The teaching load is 2-2 the first year of the appointment and 3-2 beginning in the second year, with a focus on quantitative communication research methods and specialized electives.

jobs.detailText: Özyeğin University – Faculty of Business Department of International Trade and Business – Open-Rank Faculty Position (Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor) Application Deadline: November 05, 2026 The Department of International Trade and Business at the AACSB-accredited Faculty of Business, Özyeğin University, invites applications for one open-rank faculty position at the Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor level. We seek internationally oriented scholars holding a PhD in International Business or a closely related field who demonstrate excellence in research, teaching, and academic service. Position Details •Rank: Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor •Department: International Trade and Business •Starting Date: Fall 2027 (an earlier start date may be negotiable) Qualifications Successful candidates are expected to: •Have a strong record of scholarly research and publication in international business and related areas, such as global strategy, international management, and comparative institutions; •Demonstrate evidence of effective teaching at the undergraduate and/or graduate level; •Show potential for academic leadership within the department and the broader scholarly community. Benefits Özyeğin University offers a supportive environment designed to facilitate research productivity and faculty development. Benefits and resources associated with the position include: • Competitive compensation: The University offers competitive salaries benchmarked against the European academic market. • Teaching load: The standard teaching load is four courses per academic year. Newly appointed faculty members teach three courses during their first academic year. • Research support: All faculty members receive an annual research budget to support research-related activities, including conference participation, data collection, and other scholarly expenses. • Research faculty benefits: Faculty members with strong research records may be selected for the University’s research faculty scheme. Selection takes place annually, and the associated benefits remain in effect for three years. These benefits may include 50% tuition support for K–12 education and access to on-campus faculty housing, subject to applicable University policies. • Housing for internationally recruited faculty: Faculty members relocating from abroad may be offered on-campus housing, subject to availability. Responsibilities The successful candidate will be expected to: • Conduct high-quality research and publish in leading journals in international business and related fields; • Teach required and elective courses in International Trade and Business at the undergraduate and graduate levels; • Advise and mentor students; • Contribute to departmental service and broader academic engagement. About the Department The Faculty of Business at Özyeğin University is AACSB-accredited and offers a researchoriented and collaborative academic environment. The Faculty offers undergraduate, master’s, and doctoral programs. Our faculty members publish in leading international journals, including Management Science, Journal of International Business Studies, and Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science. The Department of International Trade and Business is committed to preparing students for the future of global business through a critical, technology-aware, and inclusive approach to teaching and learning. Application Materials Applicants should submit the following materials: • A cover letter indicating the rank for which they wish to be considered; • A curriculum vitae; • Research and teaching statements; • Evidence of teaching effectiveness, such as student evaluations, course syllabi. • Two letters of reference will be requested from shortlisted candidates. Applications should be submitted to: Professor Bülent Mengüç Dean, Faculty of Business Özyeğin University [email protected] Review of Applications Review of applications will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Özyeğin University values diversity, equity, and innovation and encourages applications from candidates of all backgrounds and experiences.

jobs.detailText: Overview The Department of Management in the College of Business at Northern Illinois University invites applications for an open-rank position in the fields of entrepreneurship and strategic management. The candidate’s education and experience will determine whether they are appointed to a tenure-track or tenured position (at the rank of Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor) or a non-tenure-track faculty position. Candidates will be asked to indicate in their application which type and rank position they see as aligned with their background and accomplishments. The search committee will assess candidates’ qualifications and ultimately determine the appropriate appointment type and rank. Northern Illinois University is a comprehensive research university with about 16,000 students. The main campus is located in DeKalb, Illinois, approximately 65 miles west of downtown Chicago. Recognized by Poets and Quants as one of the top 100 undergraduate business schools in the U.S. and No. 2 in Illinois, the NIU College of Business is AACSB accredited in both business and accounting. The college currently serves approximately 2,800 students in our undergraduate and graduate programs. On campus, the Department of Management offers undergraduate degrees in Human Resource Management, Leadership, Entrepreneurship, and Business Administration. In addition, we teach extensively in graduate programs located in DeKalb, Chicago, Schaumburg, Naperville, and a number of international locations. Our eleven tenure-track and three full-time non-tenure-track faculty members include a Presidential Research Professor, two University-level teaching award winners, many College-level teaching award winners, and numerous thought leaders in their fields. We offer a diverse and collegial culture that is deeply committed to rigorous, high-quality education and impactful research. The department is tightly linked to the entrepreneurial ecosystem both within the University and in our surrounding communities, and places great value on collaboration. Position SummaryPrimary teaching responsibilities will be in entrepreneurship (Creativity, Business Model Development, Social Entrepreneurship, etc.) and strategic management at the undergraduate, graduate, and executive levels. In addition to teaching, tenure-track and tenured faculty will be expected to publish high-quality and impactful research, provide service to the Department, College, and University, and engage with the broader business community. The expectations for a non-tenure-track faculty member are similar, without the requirement for research.

jobs.detailText: DEAN, SCHOOL OF BUSINESS The University of Connecticut (UConn), one of the nation’s leading public research universities, seeks a visionary and dynamic leader to serve as Dean of the School of Business . The successful candidate will be a collaborative and forward-thinking leader with the leadership, management, fundraising, and scholarly abilities necessary to succeed as the Dean of the School of Business. Founded in 1881, UConn is a Land Grant and Sea Grant institution and member of the Space Grant Consortium. The University is the state’s flagship institution of higher education and includes seven campuses across the state: Avery Point, Hartford, Stamford, Storrs, and Waterbury, the Law School in Hartford, and UConn Health in Farmington. UConn has approximately 10,000 faculty and staff and 32,000 students, including more than 24,000 undergraduates and nearly 8,000 graduate and professional students. Record numbers of undergraduate applications and support for student success have enabled the University to become extraordinarily selective. The Dean will be the School’s public voice, promoting initiatives within UConn and across the state and articulating the School’s contributions at the local, state, regional, national, and international levels. Working collaboratively with all stakeholders in the university community, the Dean will support excellence and creativity in teaching, research, innovation, entrepreneurship, and service while fostering activities that improve the retention, achievement, entrepreneurship, and timely graduation of students. Additionally, the Dean will work with external sponsors, funding agencies, and industry and community leaders to develop research and educational partnerships that contribute to the economic vitality of the state and nation. The Dean will effectively steward the School’s and University’s resources, overseeing the management of budgets, endowments, space, and personnel. In pursuing these responsibilities, the Dean, who reports to the Provost, will work collaboratively with the University’s senior leadership as well as the School’s faculty and staff. The successful candidate will be a nationally recognized, innovative leader prepared to advance the initiatives and priorities contained in the University’s strategic plan and able to inspire and engage the School of Business community, including faculty, students, staff, alumni, and supporters. The successful candidate will be expected to broaden participation among members of under-represented groups and advance the School’s national and international reputation as demonstrated through improved rankings, successful fundraising, community engagement, and faculty and student achievement. In addition, the ideal candidate will be dedicated to collaborative governance, will possess a leadership style that values excellence and differences in opinions and experiences, will be a skilled administrator capable of building strong working relationships, and will be able to imagine new possibilities for the School. Minimum Qualifications Credentials that merit appointment for a tenure-track academic appointment at the rank of Professor or a current appointment at UConn at the rank of Professor in one of UConn’s schools and colleges, including a doctoral degree or other terminal degree in a field relevant to leadership in academic affairs and the school. Equivalent foreign degrees are acceptable. Demonstrated visionary leadership with a proven track record of successful administrative leadership. Progressively responsible leadership experience at a higher education institution, demonstrating knowledge of core management functions, experience with managing strategic priorities, and understanding and embracing University policies, guidance, best practices, and procedures. Success in building and executing a strategic and fiscally sound academic budget. Solid track record in meeting a university mission with respect to enrollment, graduation, research, innovation, and fundraising. Preferred Qualifications Background and experience pertinent to the unique programs and setting of the School, including a clear understanding of the academic vision of the university, the land-grant mission of the University, and the School’s goals and opportunities to deliver quality undergraduate and graduate education. Professional experience in or with business or industry outside higher education, including: demonstrated responsibility for organizational growth, innovation, financial performance, or the development of new markets, products, or revenue streams; or significant partnerships resulting in increased student engagement and placement, new research, or adoption of technology. Proven business and political acumen commensurate with the leadership needs of the School of Business, including the ability to navigate the organizational, political, and fiscal realities unique to a major public research university; demonstrable experience applying sound judgment; and an ability to manage change, resolve conflict, and build consensus. Excellent interpersonal skills with the ability to develop, engage, and maintain constructive and professional relationships with senior administrators, faculty, staff, students, and other individuals and organizations. A collaborative and collegial approach toward fostering partnerships within the School of Business and academic units across the University. Demonstrated commitment to increasing a sense of belonging for all members of the school, including assessing needs, developing initiatives, and applying best practices. Demonstrated understanding of the Dean’s role as chief fundraiser for the School of Business and the skillsets needed to form and maintain partnerships with donors and alumni. Varied and extensive success in securing extramural funding from state and federal agencies or foundations. Demonstrated record of academic leadership that advances excellence across the School’s core missions of research, teaching, student success, external engagement, and societal impact, including the ability to recruit, develop, and retain outstanding faculty and staff. Knowledge of AACSB accreditation standards and experience with accreditation, continuous improvement, assurance of learning, faculty sufficiency and qualifications, and strategic planning within an AACSB-accredited business school. The Department offers bachelor's degrees in Cinema Studies (with tracks in Production and Critical Studies) and Communication (with tracks in Corporate Communication, Design and Digital Media, Journalism, and Media Studies). The Department has a strong commitment to interdisciplinary inquiry and welcomes candidates whose work crosses traditional boundaries. We seek a candidate with the range to teach across both production and critical studies, grounded in a strong command of film and media history and theory. Given the rapidly evolving digital media landscape, the ideal candidate engages with diverse modes of production and brings a deep understanding of the craft alongside its social, cultural, political, and aesthetic dimensions. Candidates whose scholarship focuses on national, global, diasporic, African American, or LGBTQ+ cinemas are also welcome to apply. QUALIFICATIONS Candidates must hold an MFA or PhD. ABD candidates are eligible provided the degree is conferred prior to appointment. Preferred qualifications include: The successful candidate will have a demonstrated commitment to excellence in undergraduate teaching as well as an active and developing research and creative practice. Candidates must demonstrate the ability to teach and mentor students in narrative, documentary, and experimental film and video production. The successful candidate will be expected to teach across these areas, advise senior production projects, and contribute actively to curriculum development and program review. COMPENSATION $73,294 - $85,556 CUNY offers faculty a competitive compensation and benefits package covering health insurance, pension and retirement benefits, paid parental leave, and savings programs. We also provide mentoring and support for research, scholarship, and publication as part of our commitment to ongoing faculty professional development. HOW TO APPLY To apply, go to www.cuny.edu, access the employment page, log in or create a new user account, and search for this vacancy using the Job ID or Title. Select "Apply Now" and provide the requested information. If you have difficulty with uploading your document to the website, or if you have any questions, please send them to facultyrecruithss@csi.cuny.edu Please send a cover letter, CV, statement of teaching philosophy, portfolio of creative and scholarly work, and names of three references in one single PDF. The Department offers bachelor's degrees in Cinema Studies (with tracks in Production and Critical Studies) and Communication (with tracks in Corporate Communication, Design and Digital Media, Journalism, and Media Studies). The Department has a strong commitment to interdisciplinary inquiry and welcomes candidates whose work crosses traditional boundaries. We seek a candidate with the range to teach across both production and critical studies, grounded in a strong command of film and media history and theory. Given the rapidly evolving digital media landscape, the ideal candidate engages with diverse modes of production and brings a deep understanding of the craft alongside its social, cultural, political, and aesthetic dimensions. Candidates whose scholarship focuses on national, global, diasporic, African American, or LGBTQ+ cinemas are also welcome to apply. QUALIFICATIONS Candidates must hold an MFA or PhD. ABD candidates are eligible provided the degree is conferred prior to appointment. Preferred qualifications include: The successful candidate will have a demonstrated commitment to excellence in undergraduate teaching as well as an active and developing research and creative practice. Candidates must demonstrate the ability to teach and mentor students in narrative, documentary, and experimental film and video production. The successful candidate will be expected to teach across these areas, advise senior production projects, and contribute actively to curriculum development and program review. We also provide mentoring and support for research, scholarship, and publication as part of our commitment to ongoing faculty professional development. Send job Job Details Assistant Professor in Media Studies The Department of Communication Studies in the College of Arts and Sciences at the University of Alabama at Birmingham (UAB) invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track Assistant Professor in Media Studies to begin August 2027. We seek applications from candidates with a strong background in critical media studies and the ability to teach multimedia production (preferred areas include broadcasting, digital media, film, or multimedia journalism). The teaching load will be four courses per year over two semesters (2/2). Areas of specialization may include Digital Media, Advertising, Visual Storytelling, Interactive Digital Narrative, and related emerging media fields. Versatility in teaching media courses is desirable, as the successful candidate will support multiple concentrations within the media curriculum. Instruction may include both in-person and online delivery formats. A terminal degree (PhD or MFA) by August 15, 2027, is required. Ideal qualifications include a degree in Media, Communication Studies, or a closely related field; a record of publications or the potential for conducting research; a record of effective instruction or the potential to effectively teach. The successful candidate will be expected to contribute to our department by teaching a variety of courses in our undergraduate and graduate degree programs and developing classes in their own areas of expertise. The College of Arts and Sciences (CAS) is home to 19 academic departments and six Centers and Institutes. Our 19 departments — home to over 300 full-time faculty and more than 58 baccalaureate, master’s, and doctoral degrees — make us the largest academic entity in the UAB academic enterprise. We are home to research centers, community outreach programs, and interdisciplinary cooperation. The University of Alabama at Birmingham (UAB) is a research university and academic health center that discovers, teaches, and applies knowledge for the intellectual, cultural, social, and economic benefit of Birmingham, the state, and beyond. UAB is internationally renowned for its intensely collaborative culture that has — for more than five decades — produced breakthroughs in education, health care, research, and service. UAB was ranked #1 in the United States for 2018 and 2019 in the Times Higher Education World University Rankings, Young University Rankings. In 2021, Forbes named UAB as America’s No. 1 Best Large Employer, topping a list of more than 500 public and private corporations, hospitals, universities, Fortune 500 companies and more, across dozens of industries. Most recently, UAB earned the distinction of being named to the 2025 Great Colleges to Work For Honor Roll. Review of applications will begin immediately, and all applications submitted by October 26, 2026, will receive full consideration. Campus interviews are anticipated to be scheduled in early December. All applications should be submitted online and include the following documents: A two-to-three-page cover letter that specifically addresses your qualifications, research, and teaching experience Curriculum Vitae Teaching portfolio that includes your teaching philosophy, syllabi of courses taught, summaries of course evaluations, and other evidence of effective instruction Additional materials that demonstrate your experience in media, such as creative portfolios, recently completed media projects, and representative media publications The names and email addresses for three professional references Interested applicants please follow this link to apply: https://uab.peopleadmin.com/postings/28462 Please address your cover letter to Alan Franks and contact him at alfranks@uab.edu if you have any questions about the position. UAB is an Equal Employment/Equal Educational Opportunity Institution dedicated to providing equal opportunities and equal access to all individuals regardless of race, color, religion, ethnic or national origin, sex (including pregnancy), genetic information, age, disability, religion, and veteran’s status. As required by Title IX, UAB prohibits sex discrimination in any education program or activity that it operates. Individuals may report concerns or questions to UAB’s Assistant Vice President and Senior Title IX Coordinator. The Title IX notice of nondiscrimination is located at uab.edu/titleix . A pre-employment background check investigation is performed on candidates selected for employment. Applicants should demonstrate a commitment to excellence in teaching and research and possess a strong biblical worldview that aligns with historic orthodox Christian teachings. The ideal candidate will have an earned Ph.D. in Government or Political Science with the ability to provide leadership to PHC’s vibrant American Politics & Policy program and teach a variety of courses in American Politics, such as Congress, The Presidency, Campaigns and Elections, Public Administration, and State and Local Government. Candidates should be evangelical Christians, in full agreement with the College’s Statement of Faith and Biblical Foundations Statement, and supportive of the College’s Mission, Vision, and Educational Philosophy . PHC is a private, nondenominational, SACS and TRACS-accredited institution an hour from Washington, D.C., in Purcellville, Virginia. The classical liberal arts—wed to a strong biblical foundation—are at the heart of the College’s educational philosophy. This approach is evidenced by the College’s unique sixty-three-credit Core Curriculum . PHC is known for its talented and highly motivated students and for its high academic quality. PHC is known for its strength in collegiate forensics, having won the American Moot Court Association national championship 14 times since 2004, and for stellar LSAT scores, which are among the best in the nation. The position is subject to the College’s verification of credentials, along with other information required by law and PHC’s policies, including the successful completion of a background check. Mitchell, Dean of Academic Affairs, along with a curriculum vitae, a list of three references (one pastoral), a sample of scholarship, and a personal statement of faith, including an explanation of how faith shapes your teaching in the classroom. Tenure-Track Professor in the School of Future Media (Ref.:
537177), to commence in Summer 2027 or from as soon as possible
thereafter. School of Future Media The School of Future Media (SFM) at The University of Hong Kong
(HKU) is a newly established interdisciplinary school dedicated to
advancing education, research and creative practice at the
intersection of journalism, documentary filmmaking, artificial
intelligence and the global creative industries. Established in
October 2025, the School brings together HKU’s Journalism and Media
Studies Centre (JMSC), the Division of Documentary and AI
Filmmaking, and the Division of Global Creative Industries,
creating a distinctive platform for innovation across factual
storytelling, screen-based media and emerging creative
technologies. Building on the longstanding strengths of JMSC in journalism
education and multimedia storytelling, SFM promotes an integrated
approach spanning the humanities, creative arts and technology. It
aims to prepare the next generation of storytellers, scholars and
creators through interdisciplinary collaboration, ethical inquiry
and engagement with the evolving media landscape in Hong Kong, the
region and internationally. SFM offers undergraduate, taught postgraduate and research
postgraduate programmes for a new generation of media
professionals, creative practitioners and scholars. Current
offerings include Bachelor of Journalism, Media and Artificial
Intelligence, Bachelor of Arts in Global Creative Industries,
Master of Journalism, Master of Journalism (Documentary Filmmaking
Specialisation), Master of Arts in Creative Artificial Intelligence
Film and Media, and a rigorous and interdisciplinary MPhil/PhD
programme designed for aspiring scholars in journalism, media and
communication studies. For more information about the School,
please visit https://hkums.hku.hk/ . The Position The position is open to all areas in one or more of the following
or related fields, including but not limited to: AI and generative AI in filmmaking Animation and game design Immersive and interactive media Computer vision Data journalism, data analytics, & technologies Business and finance journalism Digital humanities AI applications in journalism practices Entrepreneurship and innovation Global creative industries with expertise in one or more of the
following areas: gaming and digital humanities, visual arts,
heritage and museum studies, cultural industries, performing arts,
visual communications. Duties and Responsibilities The appointees are expected to contribute to undergraduate and
postgraduate teaching and curriculum development, supervise
postgraduate students, conduct high-quality research, and undertake
administrative duties at SFM. Requirements A Ph.D. degree in film production and film studies, journalism
and media studies, computer science, artificial intelligence, data
science, and related fields; A strong commitment to excellence in research, teaching and
mentoring; A proven track record in academic leadership and
university-level administration; A distinguished and sustained record of conducting high-quality
impactful research from publications, competitive grants and
international recognition for scholarship; Strong connections and exposure in media industry or partners
in China and/or Asia-Pacific region; Ability to establish strategic partnerships with industry and
international academic institutions for fundraising, resource
development and School’s advancement. What We Offer A highly competitive salary commensurate with qualifications and
experience will be offered, in addition to annual leave and medical
benefits. The appointment will attract a contract-end gratuity and
University contribution to a retirement benefits scheme, totalling
up to 15% of basic salary. Housing benefits will be provided as
applicable. Nomination, Expression of Interest and Application Applications from, and nominations of, individuals from diverse
backgrounds are welcome, particularly those who are interested in
contributing to the diversity and growth of the School of Future
Media. Nominations, expressions of interest and applications should
be directed in confidence to Heidrick & Struggles via email at hkusfm@heidrick.com .
Review of nominations and applications will begin immediately and
continue until the post is filled. The University is an equal opportunities employer and is committed to equality, ethics, inclusivity, diversity and

jobs.detailText:
The Opportunity The Barry S. Miller College of Business at the University of Central Florida invites applications for the Miller Technology Endowed Chair in Intelligent Work Systems, a 9-month tenured position at the rank of professor. This position is located on the UCF Main Campus with an anticipated start date in Fall 2027. The central question addressed by this chair is: How should organizations design work and allocate responsibilities between humans and intelligent technologies to maximize organizational performance? Advances in artificial intelligence, robotics, automation, and digital platforms are fundamentally reshaping the nature of work. We seek a scholar whose work advances understanding of organizational design, the future of work, human-AI collaboration, leadership, workforce systems, organizational behavior, decision-making, or related areas. This endowed chair is part of a broader investment, five endowed chairs in all, each committed to advancing scholarship and education at the intersection of technology and business transformation. The Miller Chairs are not organized around traditional academic disciplines, but around consequential problems emerging from the intersection of technology, organizations, and markets. Miller Chairs are intended for scholars whose work has shaped—or has the clear potential to shape—how organizations function in a technology-driven economy. The successful candidate will play a central role in shaping the intellectual direction of the College’s technology-focused initiatives and will contribute to the School of Technology Leadership and Innovation (STLI), a university-wide initiative focused on translating advances in technology into organizational capability, market innovation, and executive practice. The UCF College of Business is one of the largest business schools in the United States and is located in Orlando, one of the nation’s fastest growing and most dynamic economic regions. UCF is a Carnegie R1 institution and is recognized for its leadership in innovation, partnerships, and its identity as Florida’s Technology University. The college is actively investing in initiatives that position it at the forefront of technology-enabled business education, including interdisciplinary programs, applied research collaborations, and new models of engagement with industry. Responsibilities include: Serve as an intellectual architect for the college’s Intelligent Work Systems initiative by building collaborations among faculty, industry, and government that establish UCF as a national leader in the field. Demonstrate ability to translate scholarly expertise into organizational practice through industry partnerships, executive education, public engagement, policy influence, or other mechanisms that create measurable impact. Conduct high-impact research on how organizations design and manage the interaction between people, technology, and decision systems. Contribute to the development of new academic programs and executive offerings aligned with the College’s technology focus. Minimum Qualifications: Ph.D. in business, economics, information systems, engineering, computer science, psychology, or a closely related field from an AACSB-accredited (or equivalent) institution at time of application. A record of scholarly achievement sufficient to qualify for appointment with tenure at the rank of Full Professor in the College of Business. Demonstrated impact in research related to organizational design, leadership, decision-making, or technology-enabled work systems. Evidence of an active and sustained research agenda with publications in leading peer-reviewed journals. Experience teaching at the undergraduate and/or graduate level. Preferred Qualifications: Candidates should demonstrate a history of engaging with organizations in ways that shape practice, including through applied research, advisory roles, or collaborative initiatives. Demonstrated ability to lead interdisciplinary collaborations that produce new research, educational programs or industry partnerships. Commitment to translating scholarship into executive education and organizational capability. A record of leadership in

jobs.snippet: MacEwan University is where caring faculty help people connect their passions to their future paths. jobs.detailText: MacEwan University is where caring faculty help people connect their passions to their future paths. Located in the heart of Edmonton's diverse and dynamic downtown community, and on the traditional lands of Treaty 6 First Nations and homelands of the Métis people, MacEwan is known for exceptional undergraduate learning. With its dedication to teaching excellence, informed by scholarly research, innovation, and creative activity, MacEwan provides an exceptional collaborative and supportive learning environment with a commitment to human rights, environmental sustainability, and opportunities for community engagement. We are committed to creating an equitable, diverse, inclusive, and welcoming community for all peoples, cultures, and identities. Guided by Teaching Greatness: Strategic Vision 2030 , MacEwan is focused on exceptional undergraduate teaching and bold innovation. With over 21,000 students enrolled across over 55 programs of study in four faculties and two schools, the University offers a connected, learner-centred culture that emphasizes critical thinking, community-based learning, and high-quality student support. Recently renamed in recognition of a transformative gift from entrepreneur and community leader Ron Triffo, the Triffo School of Business is a dynamic and growing business school at MacEwan University. Distinguished by its entrepreneurial spirit, strong undergraduate focus, and deep connections to the Edmonton business community, the School offers a comprehensive portfolio of degree, diploma, and certificate programs that prepare students to lead, innovate, and create value in a rapidly evolving global economy. Accredited by the European Foundation for Management Development (EFMD), the School combines academic rigor with practical, real-world learning opportunities that connect students with industry, community, and experiential learning. Building on a proud history of graduate success and supported by a highly engaged community of faculty, staff, alumni, and partners, the School is entering an exciting new phase of growth. The opening of the new 35,000-square-metre Triffo School of Business building in January of 2027 will further enrich MacEwan's vibrant downtown campus, creating dynamic spaces for learning, collaboration, innovation, and community engagement while supporting the School's continued growth and impact across Edmonton, Alberta, and beyond. Reporting to the Provost & Vice-President, Academic, the Dean provides strategic, academic, and operational leadership to one of MacEwan University's largest and fastest-growing academic units. The Dean will advance a compelling vision for the School that builds on its reputation for teaching excellence, student success, community engagement, and growing scholarship. As a member of the University's senior leadership team, the Dean will guide the School through a period of significant growth and transformation, strengthening its academic programs, fostering excellence in teaching, experiential learning, and research, and championing a culture that is collaborative, inclusive, and student-centred. A visible and engaged ambassador for the School, the Dean will cultivate meaningful relationships with industry, government, alumni, donors, and community partners to enhance the School's profile and reputation. As a champion for the Triffo School of Business, the Dean will articulate a compelling vision for the School, amplify its distinctive strengths, and strengthen its brand and reputation as a leading business school with deep connections to industry and community. The successful candidate will have a strong record of teaching, scholarship, and service to qualify for an appointment as a full professor; with a demonstrated record of progressive leadership experience within a complex university environment. They will be a strategic and future-focused leader who can advance long-term priorities, identify opportunities for growth and partnership, and guide a dynamic School through growth and change while building trust, alignment, and a strong sense of community. The ideal candidate will lead with integrity, foster meaningful relationships, communicate with authenticity and transparency, and effectively advocate for the interests of the School and University. With strong strategic and financial acumen, exceptional communication skills, and a deep commitment to student success, and faculty and staff engagement, the next Dean will drive innovation, elevate the School's distinctive reputation and external profile, and position the Triffo School of Business for continued success and impact. MacEwan University has partnered with Andrea Patrick and Cora Hui of Odgers to support this recruitment for an existing position. The ideal start date is summer 2027. Applications are encouraged immediately and should be submitted online at https://careers.odgers.com/en-ca/32011 . The Committee's consideration of applications will begin in late November. The position will remain open until filled. For more information, or to submit a nomination, please reach out to [email protected] . MacEwan University is committed to fostering the principles of equity, diversity, and inclusion within our community, and we are dedicated to removing barriers that have been historically encountered and are currently experienced by some members of our society. We welcome and encourage applications from Indigenous peoples, racialized persons, visible minorities, women, persons with disabilities, sexual and gender minorities, and members of all equity-deserving groups. We believe that the diversity of our students, staff, and faculty serves as a strength of our institution and benefit to society. We are committed to ensuring full and inclusive participation for all in our community. All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply; however, Canadians and permanent residents will be given priority.

jobs.detailText: Assistant or Associate Teaching Professor, Operations, Technology, and Information Management Cornell SC Johnson College of Business Cornell University The Cornell SC Johnson College of Business invites applicants for a non-tenure Assistant Teaching Professor (3-year renewable term) or Associate Teaching Professor (5-year renewable term) position in the Operations, Technology, and Information Management area, with a school affiliation in the Cornell Peter and Stephanie Nolan School of Hotel Administration. Candidates would be appointed at the rank that is appropriate given their experience and performance. The intended start date is July 1, 2027. The position will be in-person teaching based in Ithaca, NY. The candidate should have extensive knowledge of the hospitality industry and at least four years of relevant industry experience in food and beverage management. This can include restaurant management, hotel food and beverage operations, catering, event management, and/or beverage management. Experience in catering and event management is preferred. The ideal candidate will possess a PhD in Hospitality or a closely related field and relevant teaching experience. Candidates holding a Masters' degree in Hospitality or a closely related field and relevant teaching experience will also be considered. The Cornell SC Johnson College of Business (established on July 1, 2016) combines three Schools: the Samuel Curtis Johnson Graduate School of Management (Johnson), the Charles H. Dyson School of Applied Economics and Management (Dyson), and the Nolan School of Hotel Administration (Nolan). It is expected that our faculty teach across multiple schools within the College of Business. To be considered for this position, apply at [ https://academicjobsonline.org/ajo/jobs/32863] . For full consideration, please ensure that your application is complete by December 1, 2026. Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position has been filled. Applications received after December 2, 2026 will be reviewed if the position has not been filled. The following materials are required: 1. Letter of interest, with clear indication of position being applied for; 2. Curriculum vitae; 3. Up to three research papers or other representative samples of scholarship; 4. Three recommendation letters; 5. Report of courses taught and evidence of teaching effectiveness; and 6. Any other supporting documents, such as hospitality industry certifications, curriculum development materials Consistent with Cornell's practice, appointment to academic positions requires candidates to disclose relevant information about their prior employment including whether they have been found to have violated institutional or employer policies related to or governing unlawful discrimination and harassment, academic and research misconduct, or financial misconduct. In compliance with New York's Pay Transparency Act, the minimum annual base salary range for this position is $105,000 - $280,000. This pay range represents base pay only (for 9 months, paid over 12 months) and excludes any additional items such as incentives, bonuses, or other items. Cornell University considers factors such as (but not limited to) scope and responsibilities of the position, candidate's work experience, education/training, key skills, internal peer equity, as well as market and organizational considerations when extending an offer. jobs.detailText:
Roberta Buffett Institute for Global Affairs | Northwestern University, Evanston, Illinois Appointment: Full-time, fixed-term postdoctoral appointment for the 2027-28 Academic Year, renewable for an additional year contingent on performance and funding Start Date: 1 September 2027 Application Deadline: 1 December 2026 The Roberta Buffett Institute for Global Affairs and the Lal Initiative in Global Entrepreneurship The Roberta Buffett Institute for Global Affairs is an internationally recognized hub for research and teaching on the world outside the United States, advancing cutting-edge, multidisciplinary research and innovative education programs. This year, we are launching the Lal Initiative in Global Entrepreneurship to further world-class research and pedagogy on international business. We aim to reach a diverse international audience of private sector and government professionals, policymakers and academics. The Lal Initiative aims to make the Buffett Institute an intellectual leader in the study of entrepreneurship from the perspective of global affairs. We will consider how entrepreneurship is shaped by, and in turn reshapes, the international system, including state capacity and governance, trade policy, geopolitical rivalry over technology and supply chains, and the role of migration and diaspora networks in transmitting capital and entrepreneurial norms across borders. Among the questions we will explore is how entrepreneurs build legitimacy and trust across borders, draw on kinship, professional, religious, educational, or ethnic networks to raise capital and recruit talent, and carry cultural norms, practices, and meanings of risk and success with them as they move between states, markets, and communities. Position Overview The Roberta Buffett Institute of Global Affairs invites applications for the Lal Postdoctoral Fellow in Global Entrepreneurship, to begin 1 September 2027. The Fellow will join a new initiative on entrepreneurship in international and cross-national contexts, with the opportunity to help shape the program's future direction. We are seeking to appoint a post-doctoral scholar interested in bringing their work to a global affairs institute and expanding their research and practice networks. This position is designed to give an early-career scholar a mix of experiences, including sustained research time, the chance to design interdisciplinary undergraduate courses of their own on global entrepreneurship, and a direct hand in convening events with renowned international entrepreneurs. Responsibilities will include one to two quarter-long (10 week) courses a year, depending upon department need; the production of business case studies to be used in teaching; and convening events on global entrepreneurship. We welcome applications from current Ph.D. candidates and recent graduates whose work engages entrepreneurship, innovation, or venture creation in a global, comparative, or cross-national context. We encourage candidates trained in social science disciplines (e.g., economics, history, sociology, political science, psychology, anthropology, geography) as well as candidates across any business-related field , including entrepreneurship, strategy, international business, political economy, management, organizational behavior, finance, economics, and information systems. Candidates who expect to complete all Ph.D. requirements by June 2027 are encouraged to apply; an offer would be contingent on confirmed completion of the degree before the appointment start date. In exceptional cases, a combination of equivalent terminal degree (MBA, JD) and work experience will also be considered. Position Overview The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center is seeking a full-time, board-certified/eligible family medicine physician with maternity and obstetrics experience to join our GME Program located in Columbus, Ohio. This successful candidate will be a core faculty member in the family medicine residency program, teaching medical students along with family medicine residents. These centers feature family medicine teams made up of physicians, residents, nurse care coordinators, nurse practitioners, pharmacists, dietitians, medical assistants/technicians, and mental health experts working together to ensure that our patients receive excellent personalized healthcare. Family medicine offers team-based services, including physical examinations, wellness care, pediatric services, care for sports- related injuries, women’s healthcare, acute care and chronic disease management, family and marital counseling, psychological services, minor surgery, care coordination, dietitian nutritional services, pharmacist medication review and much more. In addition, as part of one of the nation’s top-ranked medical centers, the Department of Family Medicine has access to nationally and internationally recognized specialists and support services. jobs.detailText: Concordia University is located on unceded Indigenous lands. Tiohtià:ke, or Montreal, is historically known as a gathering place for many First Nations and is home to a diverse population of Indigenous and other peoples. The University respects its connections to the past, present, and future in its ongoing relations with Indigenous and other peoples. The Indigenous Directions Action Plan , launched in 2019 and updated in 2021, is Concordia’s roadmap to decolonization. Concordia University invites expressions of interest, nominations and applications for the position of Dean, John Molson School of Business (JMSB), with the appointment to be effective July 2027, or as soon thereafter as possible. In a moment of great change in higher education, the JMSB deanship provides an exciting opportunity for a visionary leader in business research and education. Located in the heart of vibrant, multicultural Montréal on two distinct campuses, Concordia is the top-ranked university in North America founded within the last 50 years. With some 48,000 students and more than 7,000 faculty and staff, Concordia is a highly diverse community with an innovative approach to experiential learning and cross-functional research. Over the past decade, Concordia has invested significantly to renew its faculty, improve and expand its infrastructure, and create state-of-the-art facilities for teaching, learning, and research. Concordia’s research profile continues to grow as it fosters multidisciplinary approaches to finding solutions to a broad range of societal challenges. Concordia has over 7,000 graduate students enrolled in 120 graduate programs including 3,000 graduate international students. Concordia University's John Molson School of Business (JMSB) is one of Canada's leading business schools and is accredited by both AACSB International and EQUIS, placing it among a select group of business schools worldwide to hold these prestigious accreditations. Located in the heart of downtown Montreal, JMSB fosters an inclusive, collaborative and intellectually vibrant environment that advances responsible leadership, innovative research and experiential learning. The School is home to more than 8,000 undergraduate and graduate students, supported by an internationally diverse faculty and staff whose research and teaching address today's most pressing business and societal challenges. JMSB offers a comprehensive portfolio of undergraduate, graduate and doctoral programs, including highly regarded MBA, Executive MBA, MBA in Investment Management, and specialized master's degrees, as well as a long-standing joint PhD in Business Administration offered in collaboration with other Montreal universities. Through its strong commitment to experiential learning, entrepreneurship, sustainability, community engagement and global perspectives, JMSB prepares graduates to thrive in an increasingly complex and interconnected world. The School also delivers customized professional development programs to organizations in both English and French. Housed in the award-winning Molson Building, a LEED-certified facility that serves as a hub for innovation and collaboration, JMSB maintains deep connections with Montreal's business community while extending its impact through a global network of more than 70,000 alumni. Reporting to the Provost and Vice-President, Academic, and a member of Concordia’s senior administration, the Dean of the John Molson School of Business will provide strategic direction, academic planning leadership and administrative oversight to achieve JMSB’s vision of setting the pace for the next generation of business schools. Committed to the highest standards in business education and research, the Dean will further enhance the School’s activities and reputation through increasing funding support, working collaboratively with a range of internal and external partners, and promoting innovative approaches to achieving its mission. The successful candidate will have a significant record of research, teaching and administrative accomplishments in business education, and the ability to function in both French and English, along with an understanding of the Quebec higher education context. With a record of building strong teams, managing resources, and promoting both scholarly and entrepreneurial initiatives, the new Dean will promote excellence, equity, diversity and inclusion among faculty, staff and students. They will possess an open and collegial style, outstanding management, communication and interpersonal skills, a creative approach to problem solving, and the capacity to build and sustain positive relationships throughout JMSB, Concordia, and the local and national business communities. A PhD or other terminal degree with an exemplary record of academic leadership is required. The consultants will begin review of candidates immediately, with committee consideration later in the fall, and will continue until the role is filled. Applications should include a letter of interest, curriculum vitae, and the names (not letters) of three references (who will not be contacted without the consent of the candidate), and should be submitted in confidence to the University’s executive search consultants: L a v e r n e S m i t h & A ss o c i ate s I n c . jobs.detailText: The School of Labor and Employment Relations (LER) at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in HR and Technology within the Graduate Faculty. LER is a dynamic, multidisciplinary unit with a faculty united by a shared commitment to cutting-edge research on workforce issues. We construe HR and Technology broadly, and welcome candidates whose research addresses important questions at the intersection of technology, work, workers, and employment. Relevant areas include, but are not limited to, AI and algorithmic management; AI-enabled HRM and people analytics; the future of work and technological change; human-AI interaction at work; digital work and employment relations; and the intersection of HR, technology, and automation. We seek outstanding early-career scholars approaching these issues from a range of theoretical and disciplinary perspectives. Specific Duties and Responsibilities Conducting and publishing high-quality research; Developing and teaching courses each semester in face-to-face or online formats, depending on the school’s instructional needs; Mentoring and supervising PhD students, as appropriate; and Providing service to the School, the University, and the profession, as needed. Minimum Qualifications Applicants must hold a doctoral degree in a field related to HR, work, organizations, and technology (e.g., Human Resource Management, Industrial/Organizational Psychology, Organizational Behavior, Organizational Sociology, Labor Economics, or a closely related field), or expect to receive the PhD before the starting date of employment. Appointment Information This is a 100% full-time academic position, appointed on a 9-month basis. The expected start date is August 16, 2027. Salary range of faculty members currently holding equivalent positions is approximately between $150,000-$170,000 (plus summer support). This position is eligible for sponsorship for work authorization, except for sponsorship of a new H1B petition that would incur the $100,000.00 fee. Alternative visa categories may also be considered. Application Procedures & Deadline Information To ensure full consideration, please submit the following: A cover letter that summarizes your background, qualifications, and interest in the position, A curriculum vitae, A research statement describing your experience, interests, and future research plans, A teaching statement describing your experience and interests, A sample research paper or job market paper. Contact information for three references including names, addresses, emails, and phone numbers. Reference letters will be requested at a later stage in the search. Applications must be received by 6:00 pm (Central Time) on November 1, 2026 . Apply for this position using the Apply Now button at the top or bottom of this posting. Applications not submitted through https://jobs.illinois.edu will not be considered. We anticipate hosting on-campus interviews in January 2027. For further information about this specific position, please contact Professor Richard Benton ( [email protected] ), Chair of the search committee. You may also visit http://www.ler.illinois.edu for additional information about the School of Labor and Employment Relations. For questions regarding the application process, please contact 217-333-2137. Additional Information We offer an active and successful dual-career partner placement program and are strongly committed to promoting work-life balance and family-friendly programs for faculty and staff ( http://provost.illinois.edu/faculty-affairs/work-life-balance/ ). To find out more about the resources available at the university and Urbana-Champaign community please visit these sites: • Dual Career Program • Benefits • Living in Urbana-Champaign Founded in 1867 as Illinois’s flagship public university, the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign empowers a global community of students, scholars, and alumni to change the world through bold, innovative research and transformative education. With a land-grant heritage rooted in progress, Illinois faculty drive paradigm-shifting discoveries, mentor future leaders, and collaborate across 15 colleges and instructional units and more than 20 research institutes. The university’s legacy of excellence includes 24 Nobel Prizes and 29 Pulitzer Prizes awarded to its faculty and alumni, $755 million in sponsored research funding, and 94 academic programs ranked in the top 20 nationally. Illinois offers the resources, recognition, and reach to accelerate your career — along with a highly competitive benefits portfolio. Discover how the Illinois Value Proposition fosters professional longevity, personal fulfillment, and a deep sense of purpose in every role. This position is intended to be eligible for benefits . This includes Health, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, a Retirement Plan, Paid time Off, and Tuition waivers for employees and dependents. The University of Illinois System is an equal opportunity employer, including but not limited to disability and/or veteran status, and complies with all applicable state and federal employment mandates. Please visit Required Employment Notices and Posters to view our non-discrimination statement and find additional information about required background checks, sexual harassment/misconduct disclosures, and employment eligibility review through E-Verify . Applicants with disabilities are encouraged to apply and may request a reasonable accommodation under the Americans with Disabilities Act (2008) to complete the application and/or interview process. Accommodations may also be requested on the basis of pregnancy, childbirth, and related conditions, or religion. Requests may be submitted through the reasonable accommodation portal , or by contacting the Office for Access & Equity at 217-333-0885, option #1, or [email protected] . Position Description The College of Integrative Sciences and Arts (CISA) at Arizona State University (ASU) invites applications for the position of Director of the School of Applied Professional Studies (SAPS), a senior academic leadership opportunity for an accomplished, forward-thinking scholar, educator, and leader whose academic accomplishments merit appointment as Professor with tenure. The Director of the School of Applied Professional Studies advances the School’s mission through collaborative leadership across ASU’s Polytechnic and Tempe campuses, as well as ASU Online. Reporting to the Dean of the College of Integrative Sciences and Arts, the Director will provide strategic, academic, and operational leadership to CISA’s most career-connected and professionally oriented school. The Director works in partnership with faculty, staff, program leaders, and university colleagues to strengthen academic quality, support faculty success, design, sustain, and enhance programs, and advance student learning and success. This is an opportunity to lead a dynamic academic unit at the forefront of interdisciplinary and professional education. Arizona State University’s School of Applied Professional Studies serves more than 2,500 students through 18 undergraduate and graduate degrees, preparing them to lead, communicate, design, research, and manage in complex professional environments. Its programs span organizational leadership, project management, technical communication, user experience, professional studies, applied science, communication, and military and veterans studies, all connected by a shared emphasis on adaptability, collaboration, ethical judgment, inquiry, and applied problem-solving. Through interdisciplinary coursework, research-informed practice, and hands-on learning, students develop the ability to understand people and organizations, translate ideas into action, manage projects and teams, communicate effectively, and design better experiences, preparing them for leadership across a wide range of evolving careers. This is a full-time, benefits-eligible, 12-month faculty appointment. The anticipated start date is July 1, 2027, with the potential for an earlier start date in January 2027. Salary is competitive and commensurate with experience. This position requires physical presence on one of ASU’s campuses in the Phoenix metropolitan area. About the School of Applied Professional Studies The School of Applied Professional Studies is where career-connected learning, industry-focused education, and academic innovation intersect. Its programs are designed for learners seeking to complete bachelor's degrees, transition from associate degrees, pursue graduate study, earn specialized certificates, or move into new professional pathways. Guided by ASU's distinguished faculty, who have earned recognition both nationally and internationally, and in collaboration with industry and educational allies, our comprehensive range of undergraduate and graduate offerings, as well as certificate and non-degree workforce development initiatives, provide opportunities for personal development, career mobility, and the advancement of knowledge. This is a school with a compelling mission, strong academic foundation, and significant opportunity for continued growth, visibility, and impact. To learn more about the School of Applied Professional Studies, please visit https://cisa.asu.edu/school-of-applied-professional-studies. About the College of Integrative Sciences and Arts ASU's College of Integrative Sciences and Arts (CISA) seeks student-centered faculty who engage students in practical, interdisciplinary learning, and demonstrate a commitment to community-engaged scholarship and service. Faculty in CISA are innovators in teaching and learning, preparing students to lead with purpose and make meaningful contributions in a dynamic world. CISA is a leader in applied and career-connected learning, with continuous innovation in teaching, curriculum development, veteran initiatives, and AI integration. CISA has more than 9,500 students at all levels and 370+ faculty members with 87 programs across three campuses and online. We unders

jobs.detailText: Applications received by November 1st will receive full consideration. Michigan Technological University is an R1 technological research university founded in 1885 in Houghton. Our rural campus is situated just miles from Lake Superior in Michigan's scenic Upper Peninsula and is home to nearly 7,500 students from more than 60 countries around the world. Consistently ranked among the best universities in the country for return on investment, Michigan’s flagship technological university offers more than 185 undergraduate and graduate degree programs. Research focus areas include defense, health, energy, automotive, environment, and aerospace. The area’s waters, forests, and snowfall support year-round recreation, including skiing, snowboarding, hiking, biking, and paddling. The University is an integral part of the region, supported by a friendly and welcoming community that takes pride in being a true college town. We embrace our size, climate, sense of adventure, and originality. Summary Michigan Technological University is seeking a Tenure-track faculty position in Management at the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor for our College of Business department, with an anticipated start date of Fall 2027. We seek candidates with demonstrated expertise in Strategy and Entrepreneurship and the ability to teach undergraduate and graduate courses in Strategic Management, Entrepreneurship, International Management, and other related areas consistent with the needs of the College. Applicants must have earned a doctoral degree in Management or a closely related discipline from an AACSB-accredited institution by the time of appointment. Candidates applying for the rank of Associate Professor must possess a record of scholarly achievement, including publications and other accomplishments in high-quality journals, that warrants appointment at the associate professor level. Responsibilities and Essential Duties • Develop and sustain a vigorous research program with national visibility. • Contribute effectively to undergraduate and graduate teaching through a student-centric, experiential approach in both the on-campus and online modalities. • Constructively and actively engage in service activities at the departmental, college, university, and professional levels. Required Education, Certifications, Licensures • PhD in Management from an AACSB-accredited school Required Experience • Evidence of research activity leading to publication of scholarly work in high-quality, peer-reviewed journals appropriate to the field of study commensurate with rank. • Evidence of the ability to independently teach management courses. Desirable Education and/or Experience • PhD in Strategic Management/International Management/ Entrepreneurship from an AACSB-accredited school. • Documented publications in high-quality, peer-reviewed journals in management commensurate with the rank. • Documented teaching experience in an institution of higher education with excellent teaching evaluations commensurate with the rank. • Documented industry experience. • Documented experience in securing research grants. • Documented service contributions at the college, university, or national level. • Evidence of serving as a committee member or chair of doctoral dissertations. Required Knowledge, Skills, and/or Abilities • Evidence of knowledge of the AACSB and its role in business colleges and schools • Demonstrated commitment to undergraduate and graduate teaching, program growth, and student success. • Demonstrated strong oral and written communication and presentation skills. Desirable Knowledge, Skills, and/or Abilities • The ability to contribute effectively to undergraduate and graduate teaching with a student-centric, learner-oriented, experiential approach to instruction in residential and online modalities. • Demonstrated ability to design and deliver an academic course in areas of expertise, in both on-campus and online formats. • Documented broad knowledge and skills across business disciplines. • Demonstrated success in, or potential future contributions to, working with people with a wide variety of backgrounds and viewpoints. Language, Mathematics and/or Reasoning Skills • Proficiency in English to teach and conduct research in English. jobs.detailText:
The School of Business at the University of Washington Bothell invites applications for a Tenure-Track Assistant Professor position in Management and Organization, effective September 16, 2027. We seek applicants who demonstrate commitment to excellence in research, teaching, and service in a diverse and inclusive academic community. This is a full-time (100% FTE) position with a 9-month academic year, 3-year renewable appointment. The successful candidate will be expected to maintain an active research program and Scholarly Academic status as defined by AACSB; publish in leading academic journals; teach a variety of undergraduate and graduate courses in management, leadership, strategy, entrepreneurship, human resources, and/or organization, based on their discipline, and provide service to the School, the University, and the community. Applicants from all research areas of management, including but not limited to Organizational Behavior, Organization Theory, Strategic Management, Technology and Innovation Management, and Human Resource Management, are encouraged to apply. The School of Business The UW Bothell School of Business is accredited by AACSB and is deeply committed to the success of its faculty in research, teaching, and service. We are well known for our undergraduate, MBA, and MS Accounting programs, and enrollment has been growing at a fast pace. Located 15 miles northeast of downtown Seattle, we work closely with industry leaders, many of whom are headquartered in the region, as well as smaller, innovative, and rapidly growing companies in software, retail, medical equipment, biotechnology, electronics, and aerospace sectors. Our students are drawn from and work in companies such as Alaska Airlines, Amazon, Amgen, Boeing, Costco, Expedia, Google, ICOS, Meta, Microsoft, Nintendo, Nvidia, Phillips, PACCAR, REI, Starbucks, Symetra, T-Mobile, Tableau, and Zillow, as well as in local, State, and Federal government. The School’s Management and Organization faculty (Stephen Jones, Sophie Leroy, Misha Mariam, Denis Trapido, Vivian Xiao) are active scholars whose work has been published in leading journals including the Academy of Management Journal , Academy of Management Annals , American Journal of Sociology , Administrative Science Quarterly , Journal of Applied Psychology , Journal of Management , Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes , Organization Science , Personnel Psychology , Research Policy, and Strategic Management Journal . Faculty regularly serve on editorial boards of journals such as the Academy of Management Journal , Organization Science, Journal of Business and Psychology, and more . The School of Business is an undepartmentalized School and encourages collegiality across the entire faculty. Faculty members should expect to interact with colleagues from other business disciplines. As part of UW’s tri-campus system, faculty members have complete access to the computing and library resources of the University of Washington. University of Washington Bothell Located in the heart of the Puget Sound region, the University of Washington Bothell is one of the most dynamic public universities in the state of Washington. UW Bothell is a student-centered campus known for engaging students through classes, team projects, and research in which students connect what they learn or create in the classroom with the broader community. This is achieved through close relationships with faculty members as teachers and mentors, and staff dedicated to student success. The academic work of the campus focuses on cross-disciplinary research, connected learning, and community engagement, and prepares students for leadership in the state of Washington and beyond. The campus offers more than 55 undergraduate and graduate degree programs in five schools. Current UW Bothell enrollment is over 6,000 students. More than 90% of undergraduates are from Washington State, and approximately 40% are first-generation college attendees. Areas may include, but are not limited to, the following: • Innovative approaches to funding, producing, exhibiting and distributing film, TV, video, music, and/or news • Emerging and experimental approaches to journalism • Media startups • New genres and methods of storytelling • Public-facing collaborative work • Influencer, platform, and social media studies • Artificial intelligence and generative media • Gaming and game development • Changing structures and processes in media industries This position offers established journalism and creative media scholars the resources and collaborative opportunities needed to take their research or creative endeavors to a higher level. Send job Job Details The Department of Organizational Sciences and Communication (OSC) at the George Washington University invites applications for an Assistant Professor in Communication to begin as early as Fall 2027. This is a renewable three-year specialized service position that focuses on teaching and service. OSC is a multidisciplinary department in the Columbian College of Arts and Sciences that offers degree programs in Communication, Organizational Sciences, and Industrial and Organizational Psychology. The Communication program offers a selective undergraduate Communication major, minors in Communication and in Organizational Communication, and a Master’s degree in Communication Management. For more information about the Department and program, visit https://orgsciandcomm.columbian.gwu.edu In order to maximize the integrative capabilities of the potential hire, we seek a scholar with a focus on any aspect of communication including, but not limited to, organizational communication, interpersonal communication, strategic communication, corporate and social responsibility, small group, social media, social networks, intercultural communication, and related areas. These are all areas for possible integrative connections with current OSC faculty in multiple programs that build on current and future strategic objectives . The successful candidate will teach courses that may include research methods or a senior seminar culminating in a capstone thesis, as well as other courses related to their experience and interests. Basic Qualifications: The successful applicant will have earned a PhD in Communication or a closely related field before starting the position. ABD candidates will be considered but must complete all doctoral requirements by date of appointment. Applicants must demonstrate teaching excellence as evidenced by teaching evaluations. We seek an exemplary teacher and teaching mentor who offers the greatest integration and extension of departmental expertise and offerings. The new faculty member will be expected to focus on teaching both undergraduate and graduate courses and take an active leadership role in the administration of the Communication program, such as serving as an under/graduate program director or advisor. The successful applicant would provide continuity and support for our large undergraduate Communication offerings, integrate and extend faculty teaching expertise in areas critical to the Department, and complement existing faculty resources in terms of curricular needs. Review of applications will begin on November 2, 2026, and continue until the position is filled. Please complete an online faculty application at https://www.gwu.jobs/postings/128937 and upload a letter of interest, curriculum vitae, a statement of teaching interest (addressing teaching philosophy, experience, and courses taught), teaching evaluations, a summary of administrative experience and interests (upload as other), and contact information for three (3) professional references. Only complete applications will be considered. Questions regarding the position may be directed to the Chair of the search committee, Dr. Meina Liu ( meinaliu@gwu.edu ). The Department is conveniently located in the Foggy Bottom area of Washington, D.C., just steps from some of the world’s great institutions, such as the Kennedy Center for the Arts, the Smithsonian, and the White House. The George Washington University is an Equal Opportunity employer that does not unlawfully discriminate in any of its programs or activities on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity expression, or on any other basis prohibited by applicable law. Employment offers are contingent on the satisfactory outcome of a standard background screening. Daniels, Jr. School of Business at Purdue University is seeking a faculty member in the Strategic Management Area at the Clinical Assistant Professor rank to begin August 12, 2025. Applicants should provide a cover letter, curriculum vitae, evidence of teaching performance if available, evidence of engagement with companies, any research papers if available, and three letters of recommendation. For more information on the Strategic Management Area, our programs, and our distinguished faculty, please visit: https://krannert.purdue.edu/academics/Strategy/ As Indiana’s land grant institution established in 1869, Purdue is one of the nation’s leading public research universities. Located in West Lafayette, IN, Purdue offers faculty a great work and non-work environment. Recently recognized as one of the safest cities in Indiana, West Lafayette is centrally located to a number of major business centers including Chicago (2 hours), Indianapolis (1 hour), Cincinnati (3 hours), Louisville (3 hours), Columbus (3.5 hours), and St. Louis (4 hours). Purdue’s Research Park is home to over 200 business start-ups, many which originated from faculty innovations. For a complete list of benefits, please visit our website at: https://www.purdue.edu/hr/Benefits/ Purdue University is an EOE/AA employer.
