Send job Job Details Society of Fellows in the Humanities, Faculty of Arts The Society of Fellows in the Humanities aims to attract
exceptional early-career postdoctoral scholars from around the
world to Asia's global university. Located in one of the world's
most dynamic cities and on Mainland China's doorstep, the
University of Hong Kong offers unique opportunities to engage in
cutting-edge research through its commitment to innovation and
interdisciplinarity. The Faculty of Arts is one of HKU’s oldest and largest faculties
and is consistently recognized as first in Asia for the Arts and
Humanities. Its international outlook is reflected in the
incredible diversity of its staff and students and its
collaborations with other top universities around the globe. Fellowship in the Society of Fellows in the Humanities (Ref.: 537376 ) The Society seeks outstanding applicants (appointed at the rank of
Research Assistant Professor), with a flexible commencement date
between June and August 2027 for a period of three years. The Society aims to establish a vibrant research community where
Fellows interact with each other and other members of the Faculty.
Fellows will be expected to teach two courses during the term of
their appointment and are required to submit a brief annual summary
of their activities and accomplishments. The University of Hong
Kong is an English-medium university. A host department within the
Faculty of Arts will be selected on the basis of a Fellow’s
proposed area of research. Applicants must have a PhD conferred after January 1, 2025, but not
later than June 30, 2027. They will not be currently employed in
tenure-track positions. A highly competitive package including medical benefits, annual
leave, and conference and research support will be offered to the
successful applicants. At current rates, salaries tax does not

careers website ( https://jobs.hku.hk ) and upload an
up-to-date CV, cover letter (not exceeding 300 words), research
proposal (not exceeding 1500 words), and writing sample. They
should arrange for three letters of recommendation to be sent
directly by the referees to the Society at sofhku@hku.hk . Please refer to the
Society of Fellows website ( https://www.sof.arts.hku.hk ) for
the requirements for application documents and other details.
Application will be reviewed by a panel of scholars from across the
spectrum of the arts and the humanities. The application process closes on December 15, 2026 . Successful applicants will be
notified by the end of February 2027. The University is committed to diversity and
inclusivity. The Faculty of Arts expresslyencourages
qualified persons from all genders to apply. statuses: Job Description: The Department of Communication at Utah Tech University (UT) in St. George, Utah, is seeking one creative and passionate teacher/scholar for a tenure-track position of Assistant Professor of Communication, with an emphasis in Leadership and Organizational Communication, to begin Fall 2027 semester. The position requires a 4/4 teaching load per academic year, and the successful candidates will be expected to teach courses related to student leadership, organizational communication, and/or professional communication. We invite applicants who teach and develop research on leadership and organizational communication across theoretical and paradigmatic approaches (qualitative, critical, quantitative), with interest areas in including, but not limited to, compassionate leadership, student-led organizing, community leadership and organizing, organizational support, ethics in leadership, public relations, strategic communication (across local/global contexts), and organizational justice and activism. Special consideration will be given to the applicant with a strong commitment to student mentorship and success. Special consideration will also be given to the applicant with a with a desire to reinvigorate the department's current curriculum and design new courses related to the candidate's specialty area(s). The primary consideration for tenure at UT is teaching, with expectations of university- and college-level service beginning at the second year of employment. Maintaining an active research trajectory is highly desired.

statuses: Job Description: The Martin Scorsese Department of Cinema Studies at New York University’s Tisch School of the Arts is accepting applications for a tenure-track assistant professor position in global media industries. jobs.title: Assistant Professor in Communication Arts (Review begins 10/30/2026)

The L.A. Content Studio is one of the Cronkite School’s signature professional immersive learning experiences, exemplifying its “teaching hospital” model of education through hands-on learning and faculty mentorship. In the Content Studio, students cultivate their media and audience development skills as independent content entrepreneurs, producing video, digital, social and immersive media content; measuring content performance; and optimizing content strategy. Students work to build (and often monetize) their own independent content brands through YouTube channels, TikTok accounts, Substack newsletters, brand partnerships and more. The program’s faculty leader will nurture students’ content creation skills, and develop their strategic approach, content measurement skills and audience development acumen. The successful candidate is an experienced multimedia content creator of the highest caliber with an entrepreneurial spirit and a firm understanding of how to thrive in the creative economy. The candidate must be a creative problem solver who is comfortable in an energetic, dynamic, startup environment while demonstrating a commitment to innovation and collaboration. As a member of the faculty, the professor will have teaching and service responsibilities within the Cronkite School. In this role, there are no research or creative activity responsibilities. This is a full-time, benefits-eligible, 12-month appointment based in the ASU California Center in Downtown Los Angeles. It is not a tenure-track appointment. Send job Job Details Company Job Details The University of North Alabama’s Department of Cinematic Arts and Theatre invites applications for a tenure-track assistant professor of Cinematic Arts and Theatre beginning in fall 2027 in the area of film production. This appointment is a nine-month position with full benefits. The department is particularly interested in candidates with demonstrated expertise in cinematography and/or post-production. Review of applications will begin immediately. For full consideration, applications must be received by November 1, 2026. Sponsorship is not available for this position. The University of North Alabama, situated in the historic city of Florence, is an integral part of the Shoals, a region renowned for its vibrant artistic community and rich cultural heritage. This region boasts deep roots in music history. Our faculty position in the arts offers an opportunity to engage with and contribute to this thriving creative community, where tradition and innovation create a dynamic and inspiring environment for both educators and students alike. The Department of Cinematic Arts and Theatre is a proud member of the UNA School of the Arts, alongside wonderful colleagues from the Departments of Music, Visual Arts & Design, and Entertainment Industry. Our department is home to the George Lindsey UNA Film Festival, Alabama’s longest-running film festival, which welcomes filmmakers from across the country and beyond. We are also part of the regular rotation of universities that host the statewide Walter Trumbauer High School Theatre Festival, which brings thousands of participants to campus. The department also maintains an active production culture, producing feature films and at least four main stage theatre productions each year, including a musical. Together, these opportunities reflect a vibrant creative environment in which students and faculty engage in ambitious work across both stage and screen. The successful candidate will be expected to maintain an active record of creative and/or scholarly work while demonstrating excellence in teaching and mentorship. Responsibilities include developing an ongoing agenda of research and/or creative activity appropriate to the field; contributing to student recruitment and retention efforts; attending faculty and departmental meetings; mentoring students within the program; participating in curriculum development and assessment; assisting with the stewardship of departmental equipment and facilities; and fostering a supportive learning environment. Responsibilities include teaching a 12-credit-hour course load per semester - courses include, but are not limited to the areas of cinema appreciation, screenwriting, cinematography, film production, video editing, and film directing; mentoring students and assisting with their academic and creative projects; collaborating with film and theatre faculty on experiential learning courses; providing on-set supervision for off-campus film projects, which may require flexible hours; attending faculty and departmental meetings; contributing to undergrad curriculum development; contributing to potential graduate-level courses and curriculum; managing department equipment and facilities with student equipment room workers; coordinating production management and safety supervision across film and theatre for departmental and student productions; performing recruiting activities for the department; assisting with the annual George Lindsey UNA Film Festival; engaging in additional duties tailored to the candidate's strengths and departmental needs; and fostering a supportive and inclusive learning environment among program students. Knowledge, skills, and abilities include proficiency in film production techniques, with demonstrated expertise in cinematography and/or post-production; understanding of non-linear editing systems and post-production software (Final Cut Pro, Adobe Premiere, DaVinci Resolve, After Effects); familiarity with cinematography equipment (Sony, Canon, ARRI Alexa); and additional experience with creative media and AI technology and software (ChatGPT, Claude, Midjourney, RunwayML) is advantageous. Minimum qualifications for this position include a terminal degree (MFA or PhD) in film production or a related field is required (ABD candidates may be considered but must have completed their degree by the start date of appointment); demonstrated experience in teaching film production disciplines; and a proven professional track record in film production. To view the complete job description and/or apply for this position, please visit our Online Employment System at https://www.schooljobs.com/careers/una/jobs/5497853/tenure-track-assistant-professor-cinematic-arts-theatre-film-production . Applications will only be accepted via this system. Please be prepared to upload a cover letter, resume/CV, and a portfolio or links to an online portfolio/film/creative works at the time of application, as well as provide contact information (including email address) for at least three professional/academic references. Applicants should have an emerging or established research program in one or both areas, with the capacity to contribute to teaching and scholarship across one or more of the School’s three research clusters: Global Media, Culture and Performance Studies; Organizational and Interpersonal Communication; and Strategic and Health Communication. This is a full-time, benefits-eligible, academic-year (9-month), tenure-track in-person faculty position with an anticipated start date of August 16, 2027. About the Hugh Downs School of Human Communication The HDSHC, one of the premier schools for studying human communication, offers interdisciplinary Ph.D., M.A., B.A., and B.S. degrees in communication studies. The School’s mission is to produce innovative and interdisciplinary scholarship and teaching that improves communication across personal relationships, the workplace, communities and societies, and responds to pressing issues in the world today. HDSHC faculty study a variety of research topics clustered around the following areas: Global Media, Culture and Performance Studies; Organizational and Interpersonal Communication; and Strategic and Health Communication. Our degree programs offer students a range of in-person and online pedagogical opportunities. The HDSHC faculty benefit from the use of laboratory facilities, computer resources, project support, grant development support, and The Empty Space performance venue. To learn more about the HDSHC visit: https://humancommunication.clas.asu.edu . We support the professional development and growth of our faculty and staff in their cutting-edge research to advance these aims. Within The College, our faculty engage with a large, curious student body, guiding them as they grow into socially aware, critical thinkers and writers able to succeed in a wide range of careers and to address the challenges of the twenty first century. Advancing the success of our students remains our top priority. To learn more about The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences, please visit https://thecollege.asu.edu . jobs.title: Assistant Professor in Media Psychology
statuses: Job Description: The Department of Communication and Media at the University of Michigan (Ann Arbor) seeks to hire a full-time, tenure-track assistant professor to teach and conduct research in media psychology, to begin August 25, 2027. The preferred candidate will demonstrate an innovative research agenda that advances the understanding of media psychology (i.e., uses, processes and effects) at the individual, community, and/or societal level. We are particularly interested in applicants who use innovative methods and approaches in their research and teaching, including experiments, surveys, content analysis, meta-analysis, computational methods, psychophysiological methods, neuroimaging or other social scientific techniques. Scholars utilizing a range of methods, and/or who supplement quantitative methods with qualitative approaches, are welcome. The ideal candidate will provide graduate and undergraduate students with the theoretical and methodological foundations to explore how individuals and groups of people interact with, and are affected by, mediated communication. This may include the processes and effects of media use in relation to a person’s identity, attention, stage of development, or other contextual factors; choices for exposure; and how people’s emotions, cognition and perceptions interact with media—both as recipients and as active users. All areas of media psychology will be considered. This could include scholarship on media choice; psychological antecedents and consequences of media use; representations of gender and/or sexuality and their consequences; representations of race and ethnicity and their consequences; media uses and effects among members of understudied and/or marginalized groups; media uses and effects through the life course; media effects on health, risk, and environmental behavior; media effects on cognitive processing and learning; media and children; media and well-being; new and emerging media (e.g., social media, virtual reality, AI, etc.).

With traditional strengths in arts, business, social sciences, and interdisciplinary studies, the University aims to equip students with practical knowledge and critical thinking skills to thrive in the future. Subsequent to the establishment of the School of Data Science and LUIAS, Lingnan University is transforming into a hub for global leaders to develop and promote human-centric technology and social policies. Further information about Lingnan University is available at https://www.ln.edu.hk/ . Applications are now invited for the following post: Research Assistant Professor Department of Digital Arts and Creative Industries ( Post Ref.: 26/206) The Department of Digital Arts and Creative Industries (DACI) provides conceptual and practical training for students seeking careers in the burgeoning creative and cultural industries in Hong Kong, Greater Bay Area, and beyond. The Department offers three BA (Hon) programmes (Animation and Digital Arts; Film and Visual Arts; Creative Media Industries) and two MA programmes (Creative and Media Industries; Curating and Art History). The appointee will teach a wide range of subjects including animation, digital arts and immersive media, film and media studies, art history and curation. For more information about the programmes, please visit https://www.ln.edu.hk/daci/ . DACI is inviting applications for fixed-term position of Research Assistant Professor to contribute to teaching and development of the Taught Master Programmes: MA in Curating and Art History (MACAH) and MA in Creative and Media Industries (MACMI). The appointee is expected to: i) teach courses in two of the following areas: art history, curating, media and creative industries; ii) student recruitment and admission, and iii) contribute to the research productivity of the Department and apply for RGC grants. Requirements Applicants for the position should have: A PhD degree in art history, museum studies, or creative/media industries; Good track record of referred publications, awards or competitive grants; Experience or strong capability in teaching postgraduate courses and supervising student capstone projects; Familiarity with regional creative landscapes, including East Asian art, media, and creative industries. Ability to teach material culture, art and aesthetics, East Asian creative industries or AI and creative industries will have an advantage. Candidates should have obtained / been conferred a PhD degree or an equivalent qualification for no more than five years prior to the commencement of the appointment. Appointment The conditions of appointment will be competitive. The remuneration will be commensurate with qualifications and experience. Fringe benefits include annual leave, medical and dental benefits, mandatory provident fund, gratuity, and incoming passage and baggage allowance for the eligible appointee. Application Procedure (online application only) Please click "Apply Now" to submit your application. Personal data collected will be used for recruitment purposes only. We are an equal opportunities employer. Review of applications will continue until the post is filled. Qualified candidates are advised to submit their applications early for consideration. The University reserves the right not to make an appointment for the post advertised, or to fill the post by invitation or by search. We regret that only shortlisted candidates will be notified. MCC is an associate degree-granting institution of higher education and an applied technology leader for high-tech, hands-on training. With nearly a 100-year history of academic excellence, MCC is a public community college accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. With robust student success support, free tutoring, 20 athletic teams, events, clubs, and activities, MCC has an annual, full-time equated student enrollment of approximately 2,300 and an unduplicated headcount of 5,100. The College also offers 52 Associate degree programs and 24 certificate programs. Muskegon Community College also operates the Sturrus Technology Center and Fab Lab in downtown Muskegon and extension centers in Ottawa and Newaygo Counties. Living in Muskegon County Muskegon County residents enjoy 26 miles of sugar-sand beaches along Lake Michigan’s shoreline, as well as one of America’s only luge tracks at the Muskegon Luge Adventure Sports Park and the regionally popular Michigan’s Adventure Amusement & Water Park. An outdoor recreation hub with three state parks and swimming, fishing and boating on its many lakes and rivers, the Muskegon area offers dynamic downtown and beachfront restaurant and entertainment venues. The Muskegon Farmer’s Market is the second largest in Michigan. Cruise ships dock in Muskegon, while a high-speed ferry connects the city to Milwaukee. jobs.detailText: The School of Business, Department of Management, Marketing, and Technology at the University of Arkansas at Little Rock (UA Little Rock) invites applications for an Assistant Professor of Management position (P00001202/R0089401). This is a 9-month tenure track faculty position to begin August 1, 2027. The School of Business is located in the economic heart of the state. Our students benefit from the School’s strategic partnerships with major corporations in Arkansas, as well as entrepreneurial ventures and government agencies. This gives our student unparalleled advantages for real-world opportunities and internships with top leaders in business and government. UA Little Rock’s School of Business offers eight undergraduate and two graduate degree programs as well as several minors and certificate programs across two departments, Department of Accounting, Economics, and Finance and Department of Management, Marketing, and Technology. AACSB accredited; for more information related to the School of Business, please visit https://ualr.edu/business/. The Department of Management, Marketing, and Technology offers a variety of undergraduate and graduate programs that prepare students for professional jobs in high demand fields. Our programs emphasize student development of a strong foundation in technological, managerial, and professional skills. The department is made of 20 tenured and tenure-track faculty who share a collegial atmosphere and dedication to student success. Please visit https://ualr.edu/business/department-mmt/ for more information about the department. The successful candidate will teach undergraduate and graduate courses in Organizational Behavior, Human Resource Management, Team Development, Leadership, and related management disciplines. The successful candidate will also be expected to maintain an active scholarly research agenda consistent with AACSB expectations for SA faculty; publish in peer-reviewed academic journals; provide service to the department, school, university and profession; engage with the regional business community; support student professional development initiatives; building relationship with local employers and professional organizations, including SHRM and other partners. An Assistant Professor of Management (9-month) position is responsible for teaching in the OB/HR and Leadership curriculum at the undergraduate and graduate levels. The university expects instructional excellence and scholarly output appropriate for a school with AACSB accreditation of its undergraduate and graduate programs. We are seeking a candidate with Required Qualifications: • Ph.D. or D.B.A. degree in Management, Organizational Behavior, Human Resource Management, Leadership, or a closely related field from an AACSB-accredited school. Preferred Qualifications: • Teaching experience • Professional work experience supporting teaching assignments; • Record of research; • Experience in the industry, teaching, and research is preferred. Job Duties and Responsibilities: • Teach required courses per semester (fall and spring), of which 2 to 3 may be different courses; o Classes take place in the mornings, at night (1 night/week), and/or online. o During summers (subject to funding, department need, and availability) all full-time faculty members, including Instructors, may teach an additional 2 courses for 15% of their 9-month salary, over a 5-week period of time. • Serve on University, College, School, and Department committees; • Engage with regional business community; • Publish scholarly research • Other duties as assigned. Required Materials: • Cover letter; • Curriculum Vitae; • Names and contact information for 3 references. All applicants must submit applications through the UA Little Rock’s online application system. Additional information about this position and application requirements are available on the Human Resources’ website at https://ualr.edu/humanresources/jobs. Official transcripts will be required for hire. Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled. If you have any questions about the position, please email Dr. Yue Zhao ( [email protected] ). Incomplete applications will not be considered. UA Little Rock, classified as a “High Research” doctoral institution by the Carnegie Foundation, is Arkansas’s premier metropolitan university and enrolls nearly 9,000 full- and part-time students. In addition, the university offers baccalaureate, masters and doctoral degrees across more than thirty departments in three degree-granting colleges and a law school. UA Little Rock provides a unique environment that combines a fast-paced business and technology hub with cultural offerings and deep ties to the Little Rock community. Located in Central Arkansas, Little Rock is the capital city of the state. Featuring ample affordable housing opportunities and a diverse and vibrant food scene, the city is also home to many cultural institutions like Arkansas Repertory Theatre, Robinson Center Performance Hall, Arkansas Symphony Orchestra, Ballet Arkansas, the Clinton Presidential Library, and the Arkansas Museum of Fine Arts. Metro Little Rock offers ten world-class healthcare institutions and one of the nation’s largest pediatric hospitals in Arkansas Children’s Hospital. Little Rock promotes a lifetime of learning with educational opportunities ranging from award-winning K-12 public schools to private, college preparatory academies, and 20 colleges and universities. Known as the Natural State, Arkansas features 52 state parks and is populated by stunning lakes and rivers. Central Arkansas features a 34-mile recreational trail that connects downtown Little Rock to Pinnacle Mountain State Park. According to the Tax Foundation, a dollar in Arkansas goes farther than anywhere in America. jobs.detailText: The Department of Decision Sciences and Management at Tennessee Tech University invites applications for a full-time tenure-track Assistant Professor position beginning August 1, 2027. Teaching responsibilities will focus primarily on Human Resource Management. Preference will be given to candidates who can also contribute to the department's teaching needs in Strategic Management, International Management, or related areas. Minimum qualifications include 1) a doctoral degree in Business Administration, Human Resources, Strategic Management, or a closely related field from an AACSB-accredited institution (ABDs nearing completion may be considered if the degree will be granted by July 31, 2027), 2) excellent teaching and communication skills, 3) an ability to publish research in peer-reviewed journals. Preferred qualifications include 1) experience teaching in-person, online, and/or hybrid courses, 2) experience engaging students in meaningful experiential activities, 3) ability to contribute to strategic college, university, and societal initiatives, and 4) related professional work experience and/or related professional certifications. Tennessee Tech is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer. Responsibilities for the position may include teaching at the undergraduate and graduate levels and teaching in face-to-face and online environments. All tenure-track faculty in the College of Business are expected to maintain a level of scholarly activity to qualify as Scholarly Academics in AACSB reporting. The College of Business values engagement with the local and regional business communities, as well as service to the department, university, and profession. Our department is home to approximately 500 students, and we offer majors in Business Management, Business & Information Technology, and Business AI & Analytics. Within Business Management, we offer concentrations in General Management, Human Resource Management, and Operations & Supply Chain Management. We also provide graduate courses to support the College's MBA Program and graduate-level certificates. Tennessee Tech provides impact through its engaged students, dedicated faculty, and career-ready graduates known for their creativity, tenacity, and analytical approach to problem solving. As a STEM-infused, comprehensive institution, Tennessee Tech delivers enduring education, impactful research, and collaborative service that creates, advances, and applies knowledge to expand opportunity and economic competitiveness. Physical Demands: Those typical of an office and classroom environment. Special Instructions: Applicants will be required to apply online at jobs.tntech.edu and electronically upload a letter of application, curriculum vitae, copies of transcripts (official transcripts for all degrees conferred required upon hire), teaching philosophy, and contact information for three professional references at time of application. References will be contacted via email to provide a reference letter if selected for interview. Submission of materials is the applicant's responsibility. Applications without all required materials are incomplete and will not be considered. Initial screening will begin November 24, 2026; open until filled. Salary: Commensurate with education and experience. Benefits Info: Benefits include the accumulation of one (1) sick leave day per month and thirteen (13) University holidays. Other benefits include medical and life insurance (shared cost with the university), retirement, optional 401k, and educational benefits. Deferred income and benefits over 12 months.

Secondary interests include Economics and Entrepreneurship. We seek accomplished scholars whose r
jobs.detailText: The University at Buffalo (UB), the flagship institution of the State University of New York, is pleased to announce two tenure-track/tenured positions in Strategy at the Assistant and/or Associate Professor level in the Department of Operations Management and Strategy within the School of Management. Secondary interests include Economics and Entrepreneurship. We seek accomplished scholars whose research advances knowledge in strategic management and related fields and contributes to the School of Management’s mission of producing impactful research, delivering innovative business education, and engaging with organizations and communities locally and globally. For full consideration, required application materials should be formally submitted by December 15th, 2026. Faculty obligations will begin mid-August 2027. Please see this link for complete posting information. About the Department The Department of Operations Management and Strategy is home to distinguished faculty conducting impactful research in strategic management, entrepreneurship, international business, operations management, and supply chain management. The department supports a doctoral specialization in strategic management and provides a collaborative intellectual environment that encourages innovative and interdisciplinary scholarship. About the School of Management The University at Buffalo School of Management is one of the nation’s leading public business schools. The school is committed to transformative education, thought leadership, and meaningful engagement with business and society. Faculty members engage in research that addresses important managerial and societal challenges while preparing future leaders through exceptional educational experiences. Housed in Buffalo, NY we are less than 30 minutes from Niagara Falls, bordered by two Great Lakes, and one to two hours from the Finger Lakes. The area has innumerable waterfalls and hiking/biking trails, with ski slopes within an hour of downtown. Buffalo is also home to the professional sports teams the Buffalo Bills (American Football) and Sabres (Ice Hockey) and the exceptional AKG Art Museum, as well as several Frank Lloyd Wright homes. Again, follow this link for additional detail on the posting.

We seek colleagues who can contribute to the College’s research mission and degree programs at the undergraduate, MBA, and Ph.D. levels, an
jobs.detailText: The Department of Management in the College of Business at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln (UNL) invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position in Strategic Management at the rank of Assistant Professor, with an expected start date of August 2027. We seek colleagues who can contribute to the College’s research mission and degree programs at the undergraduate, MBA, and Ph.D. levels, and other areas as appropriate. We seek individuals who are interested in being active members of a rich and collegial academic community. Given UNL’s status as a Big Ten institution, salary, benefits, and research support are competitive. About the Department The Department of Management ( https://business.unl.edu/management/ ) currently includes 25 total faculty members, including 14 tenured/tenure-track faculty, and provides a collegial environment for research and teaching. Our faculty members regularly publish in top-tier management journals and are awarded for their research and teaching accomplishments. Indeed, according to the TAMUGA rankings of Management Department productivity, the department is ranked 29th on a per faculty basis for the 2021-2025 time period. We enjoy sharing our research in progress within the department to solicit ideas and feedback and regularly invite visiting faculty to do the same. The Center for Entrepreneurship, International Business program, and the Clifton Strengths Institute are affiliated with the Department of Management and administered by Management faculty. About the College of Business The College of Business drives discovery, creates opportunity, and empowers its record-breaking 4,534 students to lead the future of business. Programs include 12 undergraduate majors and numerous graduate programs, including our highly-ranked online MBA, three online master of science degrees, and two Ph.D. programs. Established in 1913, it is the only doctorate granting business college in Nebraska. Howard L. Hawks Hall, located at 14th and Vine Streets, has been home to the college since 2017. Hawks Hall features interactive learning in state-of-the-art classrooms, cutting-edge technology, and one-stop student support services, including free one-on-one tutoring and coaching. For more information, visit https://business.unl.edu . About the University of Nebraska–Lincoln We are proud to be consistently recognized by Forbes as a top employer and certified as a Family Friendly Workplace. We are known for our welcoming, supportive environment, commitment to professional growth, and outstanding benefits. UNL isn’t just a workplace; it’s a place to build your career and make a meaningful impact in Nebraska. About Lincoln, Nebraska Home to the University of Nebraska–Lincoln, the city of Lincoln consistently ranks one of the happiest cities in America and highest for livability thanks to a low cost of living, great schools, and friendly, community-minded residents. Set amidst a big sky and open landscape, the state’s capital city is simple to navigate with a nationally noted low crime rate, a wide range of housing choices, and a reliable public transit system. As one of the fastest growing metro areas in the Midwest, Lincoln boasts a growing technology sector, more parkland per capita than all but a few U.S. cities, an extensive bike trail network, and numerous options for recreational and personal interest activities. It’s easy to feel at home here. Qualifications Applicants must have a Ph.D. in Strategic Management or a closely related field. Advanced ABD candidates will be considered; the degree must be conferred at the time of the appointment start date. Applicants must demonstrate a research program relevant to Strategic Management and a history of targeting top-tier management-related journals. Candidates for this position must also have teaching experience and an interest in teaching at both the undergraduate and graduate levels. Preference will be given to candidates with experience teaching Strategic Management at the undergraduate and/or graduate level. The ability and interest to teach Entrepreneurship courses is preferred, and candidates who can contribute to teaching across both areas are especially encouraged . Candidates with a demonstrated ability to publish in top-tier management journals are also preferred. Application Process Initial screening of applicants will begin October 26, 2026, and continue until the position is filled. Access requisition F_260094 at https://employment.unl.edu . Click “Apply for this Job,” complete the faculty information form, and attach the following documents: A letter of interest that addresses your qualifications and interest in the position. A curriculum vitae. A list of three references with contact information. One document containing: i) a sample of publications or working papers, and ii) evidence of teaching experience and ability. All four documents are required for a complete file. Only complete files will be reviewed. Interested candidates may reach out to the chair of the search, Dr. Rob Campbell ( [email protected] ) with any questions. The University of Nebraska does not discriminate based on race, color, ethnicity, national origin, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, disability, age, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, and/or political affiliation in its programs, activities, or employment. See https://equity.unl.edu/notice-nondiscrimination/ .

jobs.title: Assistant Professor in Journalism, with an emphasis on Multimedia (Submit by 10/19/2026 for priority consideration)
jobs.institution: University of Hawai'i at Manoa (Honolulu, HI)
statuses: Job Description: The Journalism Program, School of Communication and Information (SCI), College of Social Sciences, University of Hawai’i at Manoa (UHM, Honolulu, Hawai’i) invites applicants for the position of Assistant Professor (F-3). This is a 9-month, full-time, permanent, tenure-track faculty appointment to begin August 1, 2027, subject to position clearance and availability of funds. The (SCI) seeks a scholar, educator or practitioner who is excited about preparing students for a rapidly changing media environment and helping shape the future of journalism education in Hawai'i and the Pacific. The successful candidate will teach foundational journalism courses and develop upper-division courses in their area of expertise. We are particularly interested in candidates working in contemporary and emerging areas of journalism, such as digital and multimedia journalism, social media and audience engagement, creator journalism, science and environmental journalism, data and investigative reporting, documentary storytelling, AI and emerging technologies, and Indigenous, Hawaiian, or Pacific journalism. This position offers an opportunity to combine hands-on journalism education with meaningful connections to Hawai'i’s professional media and communities across the state. UHM provides a distinctive setting for exploring journalism across cultures, communities, platforms, and the Pacific region. We seek a collaborative colleague who will mentor students, engage with the profession and contribute to the program’s growth.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor in Communication
statuses: Job Description: Coastal Carolina University invites applications for an Assistant Professor in Communication or a related field to begin in August 2027. Candidates must have a Ph.D. in Communication, Journalism, Mass Communication, or a closely related discipline. The teaching load is three courses per academic semester and may include face-to-face, hybrid, or online delivery formats. We are seeking excellent teacher-scholars who can teach the department’s foundation courses as well as courses in the graduate program, including communication theory and communication research. Faculty will also teach courses in their areas of expertise. Preference will be given to candidates whose expertise includes one or more of the following areas: media, social media, health communication, and emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence. Faculty are expected to provide high-quality instruction, maintain an active scholarly agenda, mentor students, and provide service to the Department, College, and University.

jobs.detailText: The Department of International Business at HEC Montréal is seeking to recruit one or more professors in international business, depending on the department's needs, with expertise and interest in major global issues and the transformations of economic, social, and institutional dynamics. The committee is particularly interested in candidates whose research addresses, among other topics, international trade, global governance, the management and strategy of multinational enterprises, innovation and globalization, local/regional and national economic development, as well as new themes related to sustainable and inclusive economic development in diverse national and international contexts. Department of International Business: The Department of International Business at HEC Montréal is composed of 15 full-time faculty members from diverse disciplines. Faculty members have published their research in leading academic journals, including Technological Forecasting and Social Change , Journal of International Business Studies , Research Policy , Strategic Management Journal , Journal of Business Ethics , Journal of Management Studies , Management Science , World Development , Journal of Development Economics , Regional Studies , Journal of Economic Geography , among others. The Department offers a wide range of programs. At the undergraduate level, it offers a major and a minor in international business within the BBA and certificate programs. At the graduate level, the Department offers a large selection of courses in the MBA program, as well as in the microprogram, the Graduate Diploma (DESS), and the MSc in International Business. At the doctoral level, it offers a specialization in international business. In addition, the Department hosts the Institute for Economic Diplomacy as well as the Chair in Innovation and Regional Development. Faculty members in the Department contribute to an integrated understanding of the transformations of the global economy, combining approaches from management, economics, economic geography, and the social sciences more broadly. While rooted in the field of international business, the Department is distinguished by its interdisciplinary approach and by its increasing focus on issues of sustainability. The Department seeks primarily to recruit at the rank of Assistant Professor, ideally a recent PhD graduate or a candidate close to completing a doctorate in international business or a related field (e.g., economics, geography, political science) Responsibilities of the selected candidate include teaching at the undergraduate and graduate levels, as well as advancing a research program in international business. Requirements: Candidates must have the following qualifications: A completed PhD (or near completion) in international business or a related field. Priority will be given to recent PhD graduates intending to begin their careers at the rank of Assistant Professor, although exceptional candidates at higher ranks will also be considered. A demonstrated record of, or strong potential for, scholarly research achievement. A passion for teaching and for engaging with students at different levels. Have an aptitude for teaching qualitative research methods. T he main language of instruction at HEC Montréal is French, and some courses and programs are offered in English. Proficiency in English is required to teach courses in this language, to communicate with non-French-speaking students, and to carry out certain research activities. The person must be able to teach and work in French after 2 years in the position. Substantial support will be provided by HEC Montréal to help achieve this objective, in an environment conducive to improving French language skills. It is strongly recommended to mention any prior knowledge of French in your application file. Application procedure: Interested candidates should submit as a single PDF document, before October 23, 2026 , including: curriculum vitae, a cover letter, teaching evaluations, a sample of recent publications. In their cover letter, candidates must describe their academic background and state their experience in research and teaching. They are also encouraged to describe their past contributions or future aspirations to internal and external community service. Three letters of recommendation must be submitted by the referee via this form . jobs.detailText: The Management and Organizations Department at the Boston University Questrom School of Business invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in micro Organizational Behavior. This position will begin on July 1, 2027, for the Fall semester at Boston University. Requirements and Qualifications Candidates must have a Ph.D. in Management or a related field by the start date of the position. We are interested in scholars whose research shows rigor and relevance, informing pressing management challenges in domains such as leadership, technical change/the future of work, managing human capital, cooperation, conflict, diversity, power and influence. Successful candidates will have published in, have papers forthcoming in, or have works in progress meeting the standards of top tier peer-reviewed journals. Ideal candidates’ research will have synergy with Questrom Institutes including: the Institute for Leadership and Work , the Susilo Institute for Ethics in a Global Economy , or the Mehrotra Institute for Business, Markets & Society and show the potential to integrate their scholarship to inform the MO curriculum. Generally, we would like to hire someone who will contribute to our community of teachers and researchers through excellence in innovative scholarship, engaged teaching, and participation in the intellectual life of the University. Research support, teaching load, and benefits are competitive. The salary range is $213,588 - $229,398. Application Instructions Interested applicants should apply through Academic Jobs Online at https://academicjobsonline.org/ajo/jobs/32808 We will review applications until the position is filled, with priority given to applications received by October 6th, 2026 . Please include the following materials in your application: (a) a curriculum vitae (b) r epresentative publications and/or working papers (c) research and teaching statements, including teaching evaluations if available (d) three letters of recommendation About Boston University Since its founding in 1839, Boston University has embraced a mission of openness and access, becoming one of the first universities in the nation to welcome all students of ability regardless of race, gender, or creed. That tradition shapes our enduring commitment to academic freedom, free inquiry, and the robust exchange of ideas. Please visit www.bu.edu/values to learn more about our shared values. We seek scholars who will contribute to our community of teachers and researchers through excellence in innovative scholarship, engaged teaching, and participation in the intellectual life of the University. Boston University provides an environment where faculty and students work together across disciplines, perspectives, and experiences to advance knowledge and address society's most pressing challenges. Boston University is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender, age, national origin, ethnicity, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law or identified in the University's Notice of Non-Discrimination. Retaliation is also prohibited. We are a VEVRAA Federal Contractor. Under Massachusetts law, we may not require or administer a lie detector test as a condition of employment or continued employment. Boston University, consistent with the AAU's Principles on Preventing Sexual Harassment, conducts background checks for final candidates for certain faculty and staff positions. As part of this process, we ask current and past employers of the last seven years whether there has been a substantiated finding of sexual misconduct under their policies. To move forward, final candidates must complete and sign an "Authorization to Release Information" form after receiving an offer to enable this background check.

The position will be based in our Cergy campus nea
jobs.detailText: Faculty Position in Information Systems at ESSEC Business School The Information Systems Group of the Department of Information Systems, Data Analytics, and Operations (IDO) at ESSEC Business School invites applications for a full-time faculty position in Information Systems starting in September 2027 at the Assistant or Associate Professor level. The position will be based in our Cergy campus near Paris, France. ESSEC Business School is one of Europe’s leading business schools (#9 on the FT European Business School ranking) with campuses in Greater Paris, Singapore, and Morocco. Being the first AACSB-accredited business school outside North America, it offers BBA, MSc, Advanced Masters, MBA, Executive MBA, and Ph.D. programs in business administration. Its flagship Master in Management (Grande École) program is ranked #10 worldwide and #2 in Asia in the latest FT ranking. The school has many strategic alliances and academic partnerships with leading institutions worldwide. A list of department members with additional details can be found at: https://ido-department.essec.edu/faculty-staff#h.y72gakf0nuht More information on the School and our Department is available at https://www.essec.edu/en/pages/departement-information-systems-data-analytics-operations/ In the latest research ranking of the Association for Information Systems, ESSEC ranks 7th in Europe/Africa/Middle East in the number of publications in the six leading IS journals (“Basket of Six”) in the period from 2023 to 2025. Faculty in the IS group (with 12 full-time faculty members) conduct research on a variety of topics, including: · Digital Business, Innovation, and IS Strategy · Artificial Intelligence & Blockchain · Processes of IS Change · IS Design, Implementation, & Use · Data Governance & Analytics · IS Theory & Research Methods Candidates should have a PhD (or equivalent) in Information Systems or a related area. · Candidates for the Assistant Professor level should have some record of publication in leading IS journals, or a promising pipeline of papers targeted for publication in such journals. · Candidates for the Associate Professor level should have an established record of excellence in research and teaching. Salary will be commensurate with qualifications and experience. The position also comes with a substantial research budget, and the school provides relocation support to help international faculty settle in France. Following ESSEC’s wider strategy, we are particularly interested in profiles with demonstrated expertise in the areas of AI and Data, Digital Entrepreneurship, or IS Sustainability/Responsibility. The IS group is committed to increasing the number of women in scientific positions. Responsibilities of the positions include research in the candidate's area of expertise and teaching courses on IS management, digital transformation, digital business, or other contemporary topics. The IDO department proposes a wide range of electives and regularly updates its course catalogue to reflect the evolution of the field. ESSEC's teaching and business languages are English and French. Prior knowledge of French is not required, and the school provides French courses to non-French-speaking faculty. There is no requirement for international faculty to teach in French. Applicants should submit their application via the following link: https://forms.gle/ioR59KmDKVk9Jdyk7 The application package must include: 1. a Cover Letter 2. a CV containing a complete list of publications 3. a Research Statement 4. a Teaching Statement 5. Teaching Evaluations (if available) 6. Contact Information of at least three referees 7. a Job Market Paper (required), and two additional papers (optional) Applications will be considered on a rolling basis. Candidates are encouraged to submit their applications for full consideration by October 15th, 2026. Review of applications will continue until the position is filled. Members of the IDO Department will be present in ECIS 2026, PHILOS/PROS 2026, AoM 2026, INFORMS/CIST 2026, and at ICIS 2026 to discuss with interested candidates. All applicants will be notified of the outcome of their application by email, and the recruitment committee's final decision will be communicated in the same way. ESSEC Business School holds the HR Excellence in Research award. As part of our ongoing HRS4R (Human Resources Strategy for Researchers) commitment, ESSEC implements a recruitment policy aligned with the principles of OTM-R (Open, Transparent, and Merit-Based Recruitment). In terms of the European Framework for Research Careers, this position corresponds to Researcher Profile R2-R3 (Recognized to Established Researcher), depending on the candidate's experience. Candidates of any nationality are welcome. ESSEC is committed to diversity and equal opportunity, and this position is open to people with disabilities. For more information, you can consult our OTM-R policy at: https://www.essec.edu/en/pages/hrs4r-human-resources-strategy-for-researchers/ For additional information, prospective candidates can contact Prof. Harris KYRIAKOU ( [email protected] ).

jobs.detailText: The Department of Management at the University of Utah’s David Eccles School of Business (https://eccles.utah.edu) seeks to hire a senior scholar in Management/Organizational Behavior – either a Full Professor or a senior Associate Professor – to fill a tenured position at the rank of Full Professor or Associate Professor, with an anticipated start date of July 1, 2027. Ideal qualifications for this position include: PhD in Management or Organizational Behavior, or in closely related field, with an established scholarly and professional identity in Management/Organizational Behavior; Established and sustained record of high-quality scholarship published predominantly in top-tier Management journals; A recent record of research productivity and a strong, active pipeline indicating the likelihood of continued publication in top-tier Management journals; Research program that enhances and expands the intellectual environment of the Department and School; Demonstrated excellence in teaching, including EMBA and MBA courses; History of effective leadership and service at the department, college, and/or university levels; Experience building positive, collaborative relationships within and across departments; Commitment to professional and constructive interactions with colleagues. The tenure-track faculty in the Management Department includes Bailey Bigelow, Bryan Bonner, Kristina Diekmann, Jesse Graham, Glen Kreiner, Kylie Rochford, Amelia Stillwell, David Tannenbaum, and Elizabeth Tenney. With a shared interest in the dynamics of organizational life, this group of scholars conducts research using a broad range of research methods on topics including, but not limited to, ethical decision making in organizations, individual and group decision making processes, intergroup conflict and inequality, negotiations, status and hierarchy, stigma, workplace relationships, mental health, moral judgment, organizational justice, workplace mistreatment, and identity processes. This work is published in various top-tier outlets. Our department values open science as appropriately applied to a wide variety of research methods (quantitative, qualitative, mixed-method). The University of Utah is located in Salt Lake City, the capital of Utah which is the fastest-growing tech state in the U.S. and home to the “Silicon Slopes” agglomeration of technology companies, including significant operations for Adobe, eBay, Intel, Micron, and DOMO . The University is within a day’s drive of five national parks. Nine ski and snowboard resorts are nestled in the mountains above Salt Lake City, which hosted the Winter Olympic Games in 2002 and has been selected to host the Olympic Games again in 2034. The American Economic Development Institute named Utah the number one pro-business state in the country, the first state west of the Mississippi River to earn this recognition, and noted the state’s leadership in economic development, innovation, and entrepreneurship. The University of Utah is a member of the Association of American Universities, a prestigious, invitation-only group of 71 leading research institutions marked by excellence in academic expertise and research impact, student success, and the ability to secure resources in support of their core missions. The University is on the rise, as measured by nearly every key indicator, from graduation rates to research funding, to support from private and public partners. The Eccles School of Business has made similar significant gains. As the University aspires to become a top-10 public university, senior faculty in the Eccles School will play a key role in shaping the future contributions of the Business School in support of this mission. Review will begin October 15, 2026 and will continue until the position is filled. https://utah.peopleadmin.com/postings/209103

Company Description: Founded in 1919, The American University in Cairo (AUC) moved to a new 260-acre state-of-the-art campus in New Cairo in 2008. The university also operates in its historic downtown facilities, offering cultural events, graduate classes, and executive and continuing education. Student housing is available in New Cairo. Among the premier universities serving Egypt and the region, AUC is accredited by the Middle States Commission on Higher Education. In addition, the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB), The European Foundation for Management Development (EFMD)'s EQUIS, and the Association of MBAs (AMBA) accredit the School of Business; ABET accredits its engineering programs; the Canadian Society for Chemistry accredits the chemistry program; and the Master of Public Administration and the Master of Public Policy programs of GAPP are accredited by the Network of Schools of Public Policy, Affairs, and administration (NASPAA). The AUC libraries contain the largest English-language research collection in the region. They are an active and integral part of the university's pursuit of excellence in all academic programs. AUC is an English-medium institution; eighty-five percent of the students are Egyptian. The rest include students from nearly ninety countries, mainly from the Middle East, Africa, and North America. Faculty salary and rank are based on qualifications and professional experience. According to AUC policies and procedures, all faculty are entitled to generous benefits. The roots of the Onsi Sawiris School of Business date back to 1947, when the first degree in economics was introduced in Egypt. The school has been accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB) since 2006, the European Foundation for Management Development (EFMD)'s EQUIS, and the Association of MBAs (AMBA) since 2014, when it became among the 1% triple-crown accredited business schools in the world. The school is a member of the Global Alliance in Management Education (CEMS) and the Global Network for Advanced Management (GNAM). In 2024, the school was ranked by Eduniversal as the best in Africa for the 8th consecutive year and 73rd globally in open enrolment in executive education by the Financial Times. The school offers six undergraduate degrees, including bachelor's degrees in economics, accounting, marketing, finance, information and communication technology management, and entrepreneurship. In addition, the school offers six graduate degrees in economics, economic development, finance, and international management, as well as an MBA and an EMBA. The school is home to 8 research and outreach centers, including the Access to Knowledge for Development Center, the Center for Entrepreneurship and Innovation, the Venture Lab, and the Al-Khazindar Business Research and Case Center. For more information about the school: business.aucegypt.edu . Job Description: The American University in Cairo's Onsi Sawiris School of Business invites nominations and applications for a faculty position in the Heikal Department of Management at the Assistant/Associate/Professor of Finance level for a fixed-term four-year appointment, beginning in Fall 2027. The successful applicant will be expected to contribute to teaching undergraduate and graduate finance courses and thesis supervision in the Master of Science in Finance. Possible fields of interest include, but are not limited to, financial economics, business finance, corporate finance, applied banking, Fintech, algorithmic trading, retail banking, and portfolio theory. The Heikal Department of Management seeks an exceptional applicant whose research complements our strengths in the department while transcending traditional research in finance. The applicant is expected to develop a world-class research portfolio and build a diverse research team in collaboration with business and industry partners, focusing on addressing issues related to emerging markets, with a particular emphasis on the Middle East and Africa regions. Applicants will also be expected to engage in academic and community development services consistent with teaching an

Photography, emphasis in AI and Digital Imaging The Department of Art and Art History at San José State University
invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor in
Photography with a focus on emerging technologies, including
Artificial Intelligence (AI), digital imaging, computational
photography, and related tools shaping contemporary lens-based
practice. We seek an artist-scholar whose work critically and
creatively engages new and evolving imaging technologies within
interdisciplinary contemporary art practice. At a moment when AI
and machine learning are often construed as technological threats
to the independence of artistic labor, we are particularly
interested in candidates who approach these emerging technologies
as tools within a broader, conceptually rigorous set of processes,
integrating digital technologies, including AI, with material,
embodied, and socially engaged forms of production. We are especially interested in artists whose practices move
fluidly between digital and physical forms, and who explore how
emerging technologies intersect with material processes,
installation, performance, sculpture, print, or other expanded
media. Collaborative and cross-disciplinary approaches are highly
valued. Located in the heart of Silicon Valley, SJSU offers a unique
context for examining the aesthetic, cultural, political, and
ethical dimensions of AI and technological innovation. The College
of Humanities and the Arts hosts an Advanced Institute for Ethical
Technologies (AI-ET) and a Digital Humanities Center, the latter in
collaboration with the SJSU King Library. The ideal candidate will
help students develop critical, adaptive, and responsible creative
practices that prepare them to navigate and shape a rapidly
evolving visual landscape. San José State University is committed
to excellence through diversity and to fostering an inclusive
academic community. We encourage applications from candidates who
will contribute to the cultural and intellectual diversity of our
campus. The Department of Art and Art History and San José State University
value institutional excellence and are committed to advancing
equity through research, teaching, and service. We enroll more than
40,000 students, many of whom are historically underserved;
approximately 45% of our undergraduate students are
first-generation college students and 38% are Pell Grant
recipients. In addition, we are both a Hispanic Serving Institution
(HSI) and an Asian American and Native American Pacific Islander
Serving Institution (AANAPISI). SJSU aspires to create holistic
learning environments that facilitate both individual and
collective transformation. We seek teacher-scholars who cultivate
inclusive, empowering spaces for mutual learning, skill-building,
and knowledge exchange for all students. Our commitment to lifelong
learning supports meaningful connections among faculty, staff,
students, alumni, and the broader communities we serve. We invite all applicants to include a Statement of Institutional
Excellence (or incorporate it into your cover letter) to share how
your lived and professional experiences will contribute to the SJSU
community—particularly in relation to student success. A guide to
writing this statement can be found at SJSU Institutional Excellence Statement Guidelines . Required Qualifications Terminal Degree in Relevant Field: MFA, PhD, or equivalent
terminal degree in Photography, Fine Art, Media Art, or a closely
related field by the time of appointment. An active exhibition record and a clearly articulated research
agenda in photography and lens-based media. A strong grounding in the history, theory, and philosophy of
photography and image culture. The ability to teach across undergraduate (BFA) and graduate
(MFA) levels in digital photography, studio lighting, and/or
related areas. Applicants should demonstrate an awareness of and sensitivity
to the educational goals of a socially and economically diverse
student population as might have been gained in cross-cultural
study, training, teaching, and other comparable experience. Preferred Qualifications Priority will be given to candidates who possess one or more of the
following: Two or more years of university teaching experience. Experience working in an interdisciplinary environment. Technical Aptitude for and Critical engagement with emerging
technologies such as AI/ML, generative imaging, computational or
expanded photography, digital video, and hybrid analog/digital
processes. Commitment to interdisciplinary collaboration within a
department that includes robust programs in Digital Media Art,
Studio Practice, and Art History; and within a college that
includes an Advanced Institute for Ethical Technologies and a
Digital Humanities Center. Experience in mentorship and student-centered learning:
Preference will be given to applicants with a strong background in
mentorship and a commitment to student-centered learning
approaches. Key Responsibilities Teach graduate and undergraduate courses in Photography and
appropriate areas of interdisciplinary art. Advise BFA and MFA students in Photography Conduct research and creative activity related to areas of
expertise

We seek a dynamic educator and engaged professional who can contribute to two highly experiential programs grounded in innovation, storytelling, and real-world media practice. Candidates with strengths in either multimedia journalism, sports media, or the intersection of both areas are encouraged to apply. This position is designed to support instruction across multimedia journalism and sports media, with flexibility in rank based on qualifications and experience. Incorporate contemporary tools, technologies, and professional workflows into instruction. Support experiential learning through student media, live productions, field coverage, or related applied opportunities when appropriate. Scholarship and Professional Engagement Depending on rank and appointment, engage in scholarly, creative, and/or professional activity appropriate to the position. Maintain professional currency in journalism, sports media, or related communication fields. Send job Job Details Te Whiwhinga Mahi | The opportunity We are seeking a Lecturer in Communication to contribute to undergraduate and postgraduate teaching, supervision of sub-doctoral and PhD students, and to undertake high quality and impactful research. We particularly welcome and encourage applications from communication scholars with expertise in Māori and/or Pacific epistemologies and pedagogies, cross-cultural communication, political communication as well as those with existing research and/or teaching relationships with community, public sector and/or industry organisations. This position offers the opportunity to build your academic career within a growing and successful Communication programme. The University of Auckland offers Communication within a specialist Bachelor of Communication, as a major within the Bachelor of Arts, and in Masters and PhD programmes. Researchers and educators in Communication have expertise spanning new media and communication technologies, Indigenous data sovereignty and governance, cultural labour, feminist media studies, social media and digital environments, journalism studies, social change, computational media, technology ethics, gig work and digital and platform economies. The successful candidate will have teaching and/or research expertise that adds to or extends the current strengths of the Communication programme. The successful candidate will be familiar with or open to learning about Te Tiriti o Waitangi (the Treaty of Waitangi) and be prepared to build or extend relationships with Māori and Pacific communities in Aotearoa New Zealand. The University of Auckland occupies a unique position in Aotearoa New Zealand and the Asia-Pacific. It is New Zealand's largest university and an international centre of learning and academic excellence. Auckland is a vibrant, cosmopolitan, and rapidly growing city with a population of 1.8 million, and is the commercial heart of Aotearoa New Zealand. We have an abundance of natural features, including stunning harbours and accessible coastline, native bush and moderate temperatures, which help us to retain our reputation as one of the best cities in the world in which to live. We aspire to contribute to a fair, ethical, and sustainable society, reflecting our commitment to Te Tiriti o Waitangi and our foundational relationship with tangata whenua. The University is committed to a culture that encourages and supports staff to reach their full potential in an inclusive and collaborative community of scholars. We welcome applications from Māori and Pacific candidates, as well as other applicants that will enhance the diversity of our staff and strengthen our links with diverse communities. The workload allocation for this position is 40% teaching, 40% research, and 20% service. This is a full-time (40 hours per week), permanent role (subject to continuation). The full remuneration range is Lecture step 1: $99,788 - Lecture step 7: $119,204, depending on qualifications and experience. We welcome conversations about your expectations and what matters to you in your overall package. Any offer will be made within the advertised range and guided by fairness, consistency, and our commitment to pay equity. Preferred start date of 1 March 2027. For more information about this role, please refer to the Position Description . We are committed to reflecting the diversity of our city and therefore welcome applications from all suitably qualified candidates. Additional Information Ngā āhuatanga kei a mātou | What we offer The University is committed to supporting your career with: Excellent research, teaching and campus facilities Generous Research & Study Leave Full range of research and leadership development programmes For more information, please visit Staff Benefits . Please reach out to Francis Collins, f.collins@auckland.ac.nz (Head of School) or Carisa Showden, c.showden@auckland.ac.nz (Deputy Head of School) for a confidential conversation. Please note that while we are happy to answer your questions, we do not accept applications by email. Job Title:Physician - Family and Community Health, Occupational Health Physician (Open Rank/Track Faculty) Department: The Ohio State University College of Medicine and the Wexner Medical Center seek an academic Occupational Health physician to join the Department of Family and Community Medicine. Academic rank and track commensurate with academic record and experience. Position Overview The Ohio State University (OSU) is seeking a full-time Occupational Health Medical Physician to provide medical oversight and care at our Occupational Medicine and Occupational Health and Wellness Clinics in McCampbell Hall. This position is responsible for assisting in delivering, overseeing, and supervising medical care for all OSU employees in support of the Service. Support collaboration with nursing leadership, hospital administrative leadership, and other leadership as appropriate to provide operational management, financial management, and leadership functions within the Service. Provide clinical and administrative support for all of OSU’s occupational health-related clinical policies, programs, and outcomes to meet OSU’s and other regulatory agencies’ workforce requirements. The successful candidate will assist clinically and administratively with the service in strategic planning related to departmental scope, services, policy procedures, and performance improvement for OM/OHW services. The Department of Family and Community Medicine is home to 83 faculty members, six fellows, and 27 residents; however, we continue to grow annually. Our diverse departments include sports medicine, occupational medicine, integrative medicine, behavioral health, health service researchers, and family medicine. Additionally, we have two residency program sites with faculty who cover inpatient service at University Hospital East, prenatal and maternity care, delivery, and geriatrics services. Our faculty is involved in medical student education through practicum lectures and rotations through the clinics. Our family medicine practices are part of Comprehensive Primary Care Plus through the Center for Medicare and Medicaid. Additionally, our family medicine practices are staffed with dieticians, behavioral health specialists, social workers, pharmacists, medical assistants, and nurses as part of the team. stories, and editing student journalist reporting in a rapidly

ambitious, long-term projects. • A track record as a collegial collaborator in a newsroom without
silos. Application Materials Apply online by uploading (a) a letter of application that
describes your interest in the job, your teaching philosophy, and
your thoughts about teaching local journalism; (b) a curriculum
vitae, (c) the names and contact information for three references,
and (d) a one-page statement that specifically addresses how you
would engage with students with regards to teaching, mentoring and
advising. Sponsorship Information Employment visa sponsorship is not available for this
position. Community Information Columbia offers small-town friendliness with big city features and

Send job Job Details The Department of Communication Sciences & Disorders (CSD) is seeking to hire a full-time, tenure-track Assistant Professor to teach undergraduate and graduate courses, contribute to the mission of the department and the university through research and creative activity, and service activities. The Department of Communication Sciences & Disorders at the University of North Dakota is seeking an Assistant Professor in Speech Language Pathology. This is a 9-month tenure-track position, contingent on available funding. The successful candidate will receive a contract with an approximate distribution of 40% teaching, 50% research, and 10% service effort in the first year. A continued 2/2 teaching load will be considered with external grant support. UND and the Department of Communication Sciences & Disorders value diverse perspectives and seek applicants to help students succeed. The successful candidate will demonstrate outstanding promise for establishing a sustainable research program that will attract external funds and be aligned with the UND LEADS Strategic Plan. The Department is housed in the College of Arts & Sciences and offers a B.A. in Communication Sciences & Disorders and an M.S. in Speech Language Pathology (SLP). The department currently has seven full-time and four part-time faculty members, and a state-of-the-art clinic facility. There are typically 100 undergraduate students, and 40 graduate students enrolled. The Department is a part of an integrated on-campus clinic, The Northern Prairie Community Clinic (NPCC). The clinic serves as a training placement for graduate students in psychology, counseling, and speech-language pathology. Students are supervised by licensed professionals. NPCC aims to serve the Grand Forks community and state of North Dakota. Established in 1883, the University of North Dakota is the oldest research university in North Dakota. Founded with a strong liberal arts foundation, it is the state’s flagship university and is classified by the Carnegie Foundation as having high research activity. UND offers degrees in more than 225 fields of study and enrolls nearly 16,000 students. It is the home of the state’s only School of Law and School of Medicine. The School of Medicine and Health Sciences has major initiatives in rural and public health, and Aerospace is home to one of the first and largest unmanned aerial vehicle programs in the world. UND is located in Grand Forks, North Dakota, a vibrant college town of over 59,000 people located on the border of North Dakota and Minnesota. Short commutes, a great public-school system, high-quality medical facilities, low crime, ample parks and theaters, and a cost of living below that found in large American cities are some of Grand Forks’ advantages. Ranked as one of the top 5 Best Small College Towns, and America’s Best Hockey Town, Grand Forks offers stellar quality of life without the metropolitan hassles.
